items.content: New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president of education, told the Times that, “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and that schools that turn off Google’s AI features “will not have access to Search.”Many elected officials, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, responded harshly, calling Google’s behavior “extortion.” Mamdani had recently announced a policy that barred 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom. In a statement to the Times, New York City schools chancellor Kamar H. Samuels said, “If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options.” Chicago’s public schools have also reportedly told Google that if it can’t provide a version of Search without AI, “the district will look to other search solutions.”In a statement to The Verge, Google spokesperson Laura Breen said, “We hear parents and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to shortcut learning, and we share the same goal: help students learn. To improve Search for the classroom, we’re starting to pilot Guided Learning capabilities in Search this month to walk students step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers. Next year, we’re also updating our approach to controls for schools to address feedback we’ve heard from educators, so Gemini app, Gemini Notebook and Search will be off by default until schools decide which services to enable. We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers.”Educators are wary of AI’s effect on students’ critical thinking skills, and some studies have shown that students who use AI generally perform worse on tests. There are also concerns about the mental health effects on children who develop relationships with chatbots at a young age. But Google is deeply embedded in classrooms across the US, which rely on Google Classroom, Chromebooks, and other services, and going fully Google-free might prove difficult.

items.titleZh: 全美最大的几个学区考虑弃用谷歌搜索
items.descriptionZh:
据《纽约时报》报道，纽约、洛杉矶和芝加哥的学校正在考虑改用Google搜索的替代方案。原因是Google表示，如果学校选择退出其AI功能，公司将禁用这些学校的Search服务。从明年开始，学校将无法在保留Search的同时单独关闭由Gemini驱动的功能；换句话说，学校若想禁用Gemini相关AI功能，就必须同时放弃Search。Google教育业务副总裁Chris Phillips对《纽约时报》称，“Search和AI已经深度整合”，关闭Google的AI功能意味着学校“将无法访问Search”。

这一做法引发多名民选官员强烈批评。纽约市市长Zohran Mamdani和参议员Bernie Sanders称Google的行为是“勒索”。Mamdani最近宣布政策，禁止2-K-8学生在课堂使用AI。纽约市学校总监Kamar H. Samuels表示，如果Google不重新考虑立场，纽约市将探索其他搜索选项。芝加哥公立学校也 reportedly 告知Google，如果不能提供不含AI的Search版本，该学区将寻找其他搜索解决方案。

从技术角度看，这一争议的核心是Google将生成式AI能力嵌入搜索产品架构：搜索不再只是返回链接，而是结合Gemini提供摘要、对话和引导式解答。Google发言人对The Verge表示，公司理解家长和教师担心学生用AI“走捷径”学习，但双方目标一致，都是帮助学生学习的。Google本月开始在Search中试点“Guided Learning”能力，不再只给出快速答案，而是分步骤引导学生解决复杂问题。Google还称，明年将更新面向学校的控制方案，以回应教育者反馈：Gemini应用、Gemini Notebook和Search将默认关闭，直到学校决定启用哪些服务。Google表示正在与教育者合作构建这些体验。

背景上，美国教育界对生成式AI进入课堂持谨慎态度，担忧其削弱学生批判性思维。一些研究显示，使用AI的学生在测试中通常表现更差；也有人担心儿童过早与聊天机器人建立关系会影响心理健康。但Google在美国课堂中嵌入很深，学校广泛依赖Google Classroom、Chromebooks等服务，完全“去Google化”可能并不容易。此次事件反映出学校对教学自主权、学生隐私和AI使用边界的关切，与Google将AI深度整合进搜索和教育生态的商业与技术路线之间的冲突。若纽约、洛杉矶、芝加哥等大型学区转向替代搜索方案，可能影响Google在教育市场的产品采用和学校采购决策。报道未披露具体性能指标或成本对比数据。

items.title: AMD’s Twitter brag that it ‘loves gamers’ met with savage Community Note
items.description: Following a post on X, AMD Japan's claim that the company values gamers "above all else" saw those gamers point out that its own CEO believes the company is more focused on data centers.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter AMD Japan's X account has been met with sharp reproach after claiming the company loves gamers and values its interactions with gamers above all else, with commenters and even a community note expressing dissent at the sentiment, owing to AMD's comments on its "data center-first" ethos and a commitment to AI that has driven the price of consumer PC gaming up to nearly unaffordable levels.Quoting a Tom's Hardware post on the X social network discussing CEO Dr. Lisa Su meeting gamers and autographing a GPU, the AMD Japan account was quick to seize the moment. "AMD values its interactions with gamers above all else," the post read, but it was met with a stark reminder that gamers don't feel the same way. The post soon received a new community note that pointed out that AMD's own CEO doesn't agree. In fact, Su was quoted as saying that AMD is now "a data center-first company," with the note also pointing to the fact that AMD's data center revenue increased 97% year-over-year, as per its Q3 2026 earnings report. That equates to around $8.5 billion in revenue, while client and gaming revenue fell 8% to $3.7 billion. Gaming alone was down 40%.At the time, Su said that AMD expected its server revenue to double year over year in 2027, with its data center AI revenue growing at an even faster rate. "As a result, we expect data center to be more than eighty percent of our total revenue in 2027 and to drive the majority of our revenue and earnings growth," the CEO said during the company's earnings call.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: ゲーマーとの交流を何よりも大切にするAMD。 コミュニティと直接つながり、その声に耳を傾け続ける姿勢こそAMDの強みです。 AMD loves gamers. 🎮November 17, 2026By comparison, the same call heard Su say that, in 2027, AMD was "planning for PC market unit shipments to decline by a double-digit percentage." With this all in mind, it's perhaps no surprise that the AMD Japan X account stirred such a strong response from gamers who feel that AMD has left them behind in search of a more lucrative data center market. AMD is certainly not alone in that regard. Nvidia, once the darling of the PC component enthusiast, is now focused on AI data center components instead. The company's high-performance AI chips are so capable that they're export-controlled, something that, among other reasons, will put former CEO Jensen Huang in front of a House Foreign Affairs panel in December.As for AMD, its ill-timed, misjudged X post ended with "AMD loves gamers." Gamers would appear to disagree. items.content: If someone handed you $8,300 every second, what would you do? That’s how much pure profit Nvidia now makes. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, Nvidia will likely have cleared $45,000 and change. It’s easy to look at Nvidia, a company that just lost its visionary founder CEO due to a series of scandals, and think that the company and maybe the entire AI industry are in terrible trouble. Perhaps so?RelatedAn overview of Jensen Huang’s messy daysJensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEOBut I want you to understand: Nvidia isn’t your average semi-successful company that might tempt a new CEO to fix things that are broken. It is a company so staggeringly, mind-bogglingly successful it’ll do everything in its power not to rock the boat. There is so much money at stake.It’s so much money that when I heard about Jensen Huang’s resignation, my first thought was: I need a way to visualize this jaw-dropping amount of money for you. I want to show you that Nvidia has risen so far, so fast, that rival chipmakers AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm barely qualify as competition now. If you’re on a desktop OS, you could mouse over each dot in our chart above to see the staggering sums. But we built another way to visualize the rise of Nvidia I like even better. It’s a horizontal bar graph that not only puts Nvidia’s revenue growth in perspective, but shows you its monster profits right alongside them — plus the world events that made Nvidia a star. TL;DR: The crypto boom and the great GPU shortage have nothing on the AI boom. Those earlier periods saw Nvidia’s profits briefly peak at $1.24 billion and $3 billion a quarter respectively, while the rise of data centers has driven them to $65 billion per quarter with no sign of stopping.Yes, Jensen may have set a trillion dollars of Nvidia’s market cap on fire — from around $5 trillion at the start of November to “only” $3.6 trillion now — but the smoldering company is raking in $700 million in profit a day on average.Put another way: Nvidia could give a $1 million bonus to every one of its 42,000 employees, every three months, without running out of cash. Or, you know, Nvidia could end world hunger or provide clean water for everyone, now that it’s making over $200 billion in pure profit a year.Maybe that’d make people feel differently about data centers? But even if we stick to self-serving capitalism, you’re probably still a happy investor if you bought Nvidia a decade ago. A $1,000 investment 10 years ago is now worth over $67,000. You’d have over $1 million if you invested $15,000 back then. And make no mistake, Nvidia is sticking to capitalism. Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress just promised to return as much money to investors as possible on the company’s November 17th earnings call. “Going forward, we intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders,” she announced. “All” is a lot more than the 50 percent baseline that Jensen promised five months ago.Nvidia isn’t the only company whose fortunes have risen this dramatically. RAMageddon revealed that just three companies — Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron — controlled nearly 90 percent of the entire global DRAM market, and those three have repeatedly signaled that they’d prefer to celebrate record profits instead of ramping up production too fast. But while their revenues and profits have been skyrocketing even faster over the past year or so, even Big RAM hasn’t caught the AI wave quite the same way as Nvidia. Samsung, of course, doesn’t just make memory — its revenue numbers include phones, tablets, TVs, home appliances, chips, displays, camera sensors, audio, networking equipment, medical equipment, and more.In the most recent quarter, Micron made $37.7 billion in profit, SK Hynix made $29.8 billion, and Samsung came in at around $55.3 billion, but they’re all shy of Nvidia’s $65.3 billion. Historically, RAM has also been a bit more cyclical: Both Micron and SK Hynix actually lost money in 2023 because they produced too much memory.On its latest earnings call, the first since cofounder Jensen Huang’s resignation, interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress reinforced the idea that Nvidia expects the good times to keep on rolling.Asked how things might change under new management, she suggested that they wouldn’t: “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual,” she said. She added that the company has secured the backing of customers and suppliers including TSMC, the all-important firm that actually fabricates Nvidia’s chips.“Our momentum is real, our demand is accelerating, our supply is growing. Our customers and partners are with us, and employees are committed,” she claimed. “We’ve got this.”Nvidia claims it’ll rake in even more money next quarter, with projected revenue of $130 billion. Profit may be proportionally smaller since gross margins are estimated to drop to 71–72 percent (compared to nearly 75 percent), but Kress said Nvidia intends to get them up as high as 73 percent next year.In other words: This astounding gravy train isn’t going anywhere. At least that’s the plan.Stevie Bonifield contributed to this story.

items.titleZh: 英伟达的崛起，可视化呈现
items.descriptionZh:
原文以“每秒净赚8300美元”开篇，称读完一段的时间Nvidia就能入账约4.5万美元，借此强调其盈利规模已到惊人程度。背景是：原文称Nvidia创始人兼CEO黄仁勋因一系列丑闻离职，外界容易因此担心公司和整个AI行业陷入麻烦；但文章强调，Nvidia并非一家需要新CEO“修修补补”的普通公司，而是一家成功到不愿轻易改变方向的巨头，背后牵涉的资金规模太大。文章用收入与利润可视化说明：加密热潮和GPU短缺时期，Nvidia季度利润峰值分别约为12.4亿美元和30亿美元；而AI数据中心需求将其推高至每季度650亿美元，且未见停止迹象。尽管市值从11月初约5万亿美元降至“仅”3.6万亿美元，公司日均利润仍约7亿美元，年纯利润超过2000亿美元。形象地说，Nvidia可以每季度给4.2万名员工每人发100万美元奖金而不至于现金枯竭；十年前投资1000美元，如今价值超过6.7万美元，投资1.5万美元则超过100万美元。

技术逻辑上，原文并未展开具体芯片架构，但核心驱动很清楚：AI数据中心对GPU算力的结构性需求。GPU的大规模并行计算适合大模型训练和推理，数据中心集群把算力变成基础设施，使Nvidia从游戏显卡和加密挖矿周期转向AI基础设施的核心供应商。其供应链和客户关系也被视为关键支撑：临时CEO兼CFO Colette Kress称公司已获得包括台积电在内的客户和供应商支持，并表示“从业务角度看，一切照常”，“势头是真实的，需求在加速，供应在增长”。她还在11月17日财报电话会上承诺，将扣除战略用途后的全部超额自由现金流返还股东，这高于五个月前黄仁勋承诺的50%基线。Nvidia预计下一季度营收达1300亿美元；毛利率预计从近75%降至71%—72%，但计划明年提升至73%。

对比数据方面，文章指出三星、SK海力士和美光三家控制近90%的全球DRAM市场，却更倾向于庆祝创纪录利润而非过快扩产。最近季度利润为：美光377亿美元、SK海力士298亿美元、三星约553亿美元，均低于Nvidia的653亿美元；同时RAM行业周期性更强，美光和SK海力士曾在2023年因供过于求而亏损。总体看，Nvidia的业绩反映了AI数据中心资本开支的强劲势头，应用场景覆盖大模型训练、推理和云端AI基础设施；但高利润、供应链集中和内存周期也提示AI繁荣背后的资本密集与周期性风险。原文结论是：这列“利润列车”短期不会停下，至少这是公司的计划。

items.title: Nvidia promises employee pay raises, equity before December to quell unrest in wake of Jensen Huang scandal
items.description: Interim CEO Collete Kress reportedly offered staffers higher wages and more equity on an advanced schedule at the company's first all-hands after Jensen Huang resigned.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia today held its first all-hands meeting since the resignation of co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. According to Wired, interim CEO Colette Kress offered more money and equity on a faster-than-expected schedule to calm staffers' nerves."So I’m here to tell you, the best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp,” Wired reports Kress said.The pay and equity bumps are set for December, far ahead of the company's normal raise cycle. Kress said that compensation and more clarity from the board were the most common topics in questions submitted ahead of the meeting. Keeping current employees happy will be one of Kress' most important short-term challenges. One director-level employee has already written to the board and top executives, warning that failure to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive could lead to the loss of ‘irreplaceable talent.’A potential exodus of talent could also spook investors, despite standout earnings on Thursday. A leadership crisis could make the company seem less stable, and Huang had placed himself as the anchor point for many decisions and the company's overall vision.Huang has expressed interest in returning to Nvidia, saying he would be "honored" to lead the company again if asked by the board. The board was clear in yesterday's earnings call that it did not intend to bring Huang back, though there is reportedly a pro-Huang faction.Nvidia cofounder Chris Malachowsky was also on the call, explaining that the company lives its values rather than simply plastering them on posters.“We’re going to be fine,” he said. items.titleZh: 英伟达承诺12月前为员工加薪并授予股权，以平息黄仁勋丑闻引发的动荡
items.descriptionZh:
英伟达在联合创始人、前CEO黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）辞职后召开首次全员大会。据Wired报道，临时CEO科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）在会上宣布，将以快于预期的节奏向员工提供更多现金和股权奖励，以安抚员工情绪。克雷斯表示，公司最重要的是照顾好每一位现有员工，让大家对公司感觉良好、不必担心薪酬。加薪和股权奖励预计在12月落地，明显早于公司正常加薪周期。她还透露，会前员工提交的问题最集中在薪酬和董事会提供更明确信息两方面。

留住现有员工是克雷斯短期内的关键挑战之一。报道称，已有一名总监级员工致信董事会和高管，警告若不能恢复黄仁勋的CEO职位，公司可能失去“不可替代的人才”。潜在的人才外流也可能令投资者不安，尽管英伟达周四公布了亮眼财报。领导层危机可能让公司显得不够稳定，而黄仁勋此前将自己置于许多决策和公司整体愿景的“锚点”位置。黄仁勋已表达回归兴趣，称若董事会邀请，他将“荣幸”再次领导公司。但董事会在前一日财报电话会上明确表示不打算让黄仁勋回归，不过据报道公司内部存在支持黄仁勋的派系。联合创始人克里斯·马拉霍夫斯基（Chris Malachowsky）也在电话会上表示，公司是践行价值观，而不是把价值观贴在海报上，并称“我们会没事的”。

该报道聚焦英伟达领导层交接、薪酬安抚和人才保留，未涉及具体芯片产品或技术参数。对AI芯片公司而言，核心资产高度依赖关键人才和路线图连续性，此次事件的关键影响在于员工士气、人才流失风险以及投资者对公司稳定性的判断。

items.content: If the glorious AI revolution rests entirely on the well-being of one man, AI is perhaps not as robust a technology as I had previously been led to believe. Nonetheless, chunks of Silicon Valley are now insisting he is indispensable. For instance, if Elon Musk is telling the truth, then Jensen Huang (the former CEO of Nvidia, a company with a market cap of about $3 trillion) has been making deals that were “a handshake with Jensen” with suppliers — “not a written contract,” Musk wrote.Fascinating stuff to tell shareholders. But after listening to Nvidia’s first earnings call with its new CEO, Colette Kress, I do think something may have shifted. In her former role as CFO, Kress generally told Huang to stop spending so much money on financing its customers, because telling the CEO to stop spending so much goddamn money is the CFO’s job. Apparently he belittled her about this, but that’s the CEO–CFO relationship, baby! Anyway she’s the boss now, at least temporarily. I think it’s reasonable to assume that though Nvidia has for years been the AI industry’s sugar daddy, without Huang and his handshakes in the picture, it may be less liberal with its cash.Kress shot down the idea that Huang’s departure would lead to a brain drain within NvidiaKress’ job was never going to be easy. Even without tantrums from the likes of Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Musk, both of whom seem to have a lot of free time for guys who are ostensibly running multibillion-dollar companies, having to steer a company after an event on the scale of Huang’s meltdown is a miserable task. But this woman also is now having to deal with a bunch of guys publicly insisting that Huang was the only reason Nvidia succeeded. It amused me on the call that she did the thing I often do when men decide they can bully me, which is to tap in another man who is theoretically or actually in charge of me — and so on the call, Nvidia board Chair Harvey C. Jones politely told these losers to get bent. The board does not intend to reinstate Huang, and the company won’t be taking questions about him.On the call, Kress pointedly noted that Nvidia’s agreements with suppliers last through the end of the decade, so I suppose we must entertain the possibility that when it comes to the handshake deals, Musk is, once again, lying. This is an important thing, though — as SemiAnalysis noted in its bizarrely conspiratorial post on the situation, Nvidia is successful because it has choked off the supply chain.Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46Kress also shot down the idea that Huang’s departure would lead to a brain drain within Nvidia, or the kind of open internal revolt that got Sam Altman reinstated at OpenAI during “the blip” in 2023. She told investors that “our employees, we believe, are committed. They are committed to doing their life’s work at Nvidia.” Nvidia’s employees have “been working seamlessly on what they need to complete,” she added. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual.” I’m sure we’ll hear more about this in the coming days, but unlike with Altman, Huang resigned, and we all know why. And while some employees support reinstating Huang, I notice that there’s a real dearth of “we’ll quit with him” in those sentiments.I don’t think this is going to shut the Branch Nvidians up, but I do think the board doesn’t have another choice here. Hilariously, we learned this weekend that Nvidia did not buy complete directors’ and officers’ insurance. While the individual executives’ and board members’ personal assets are shielded from lawsuits that stem from its executives’ behavior, the company is not. So if someone, or perhaps several someones, were to file a suit because of, say, Huang’s personal life and its damaging effects on the stock price, Nvidia itself is on the hook.The scandal isn’t mainly about the affairs, as much fun as we all have been having with themThis is to say nothing of the Securities and Exchange Commission’s investigation — which, given how cliqued up Huang was with President Donald Trump, may be investigating on his behalf rather than investigating him — or the California attorney general going on Bloomberg TV to say that he was going to start kicking the tires on an investigation, or Huang and general counsel Tim Teter’s upcoming congressional testimony. The three actual lawyers left at the Department of Justice may be doing their own investigation, too. Elizabeth Warren seems mad. Marco Rubio’s name has been publicly attached in stories on the leaks, which makes me a little suspicious about who’s been doing the leaking.A reminder: The scandal isn’t mainly about the affairs, as much fun as we all have been having with them. It is about Nvidia customers allegedly circumventing a ban on selling chips to China. The scandal is already big enough that US policy has been altered; the Department of Commerce informed us all on November 16th that there were new restrictions on selling chips to countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. Also, data centers around the world need licenses from the US to lease compute to companies headquartered in China.“No one could tell them ‘no’ or put them in their place.”You may be wondering how these restrictions will affect Nvidia’s sales. The company also addressed this, though somewhat obliquely: It raised its forecast, saying that revenue will grow by 75 percent next year. Still, given that Singapore alone was responsible for $104 billion of revenue in 2025, I am curious about the number; at the time, it was the second-biggest geographic area by revenue, dwarfed only by the US. I can’t tell you how much Singaporean sales matter to Nvidia now, because around the time that Singaporean sales reportedly started to represent half the company’s revenue, Nvidia switched its reporting methodology. The company had previously noted that “most shipments associated with Singapore revenue were to locations other than Singapore and shipments to Singapore were insignificant.” Notably, Megaspeed had a Singapore address — and was the subject of a truncated Commerce Department investigation into whether its chips were being diverted to China. Fun stuff!You know what else is fun? Jensen Huang’s children are still at the company, at least as far as anyone knows. His daughter Madison, described as Huang’s “chief of staff” by The New York Times, even helped direct Nvidia’s response to inquiries about Megaspeed, which have been mounting now for a year, the Financial Times reported. Her husband, Nico Caprez, “was promoted to a role that covered international deals with cloud computing clients in Asia” around the time those inquiries were getting started. “They had a lot of power and influence and were allowed to operate unchecked,” an anonymous source told the FT. “No one could tell them ‘no’ or put them in their place.”His kids — one of them, Spencer, ran a bar before his role at Nvidia — likely haven’t endeared themselves to their colleagues, based on some of the reporting now trickling out about them. What was Spencer doing at Nvidia? Unknown. “Some executives said they had never encountered Spencer Huang in the course of business,” The Wall Street Journal wrote.As a person who loves mess, I think the Branch Nvidians should keep this shit comingEmploying the CEO’s relatives was already a governance risk. If the outside agitation continues to reinstate Jensen Huang, there are three key lambs that Nvidia can slaughter, and all of them are his relatives. I suppose the thing I find most astonishing is that Huang doesn’t see the writing on the wall; he has posted that if “the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” The post was met with, among other things, Altman posting a green heart in response.Now, as a person who loves mess, I think the Branch Nvidians should keep this shit coming. I mean, Huang can nominate two people to the board of directors before the company’s shareholder meeting next year. Let’s have a stupid proxy fight and see what else leaks about Huang’s leadership and children! Of course, that will be difficult for Kress to manage — but that’s I guess what she’s getting paid for.Up until now, Kress had been trying to rein in Huang’s spending on the AI ecosystem — financing, investments, and so on — in a huge swath of companies, according to stories in The Information and The Wall Street Journal. According to the Journal’s story, Huang noted that the vaunted deals he’d made with suppliers “were coming at him like an ‘avalanche,’” while “major cloud providers were running away from Nvidia.” This does explain Nvidia’s role as the sugar daddy for the neocloud industry. Kress reportedly pushed back on some of its agreements, apparently significantly downsizing a financial commitment to OpenAI among other things. Now, while she’ll be spending plenty of her time managing the fallout from Huang’s departure, she won’t be directly fighting with him over Nvidia’s finances.It publicly tells us there are limitations on what Nvidia is willing to supportOn the earnings call, analyst Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein Research asked about a new paragraph he’d noticed in the earnings release about neoclouds. Nvidia had been supplying guarantees to some neoclouds by saying it would purchase compute if no one else would. The new paragraph reads, in part, “Our commitments take effect only if the neoclouds secure financing to purchase the data center infrastructure products and the related compute capacity is deployed, made operational, and accepted by us.” Kress clarified that this meant that if neoclouds’ buildout was delayed — or they otherwise had a challenge in building the warehouse to stick the chips in — Nvidia’s guarantee “doesn’t exist anymore,” she said. “Is it new? No. Did we change anything? No,” she said.I have no way of knowing if this language had been ready to go in the press release before Huang resigned, but it does seem notable all the same. It publicly tells us there are limitations on what Nvidia is willing to support. And knowing Kress wanted Huang to spend less on this stuff, I think it tees us up for an interesting period. Passing under the radar last week were some indications that the Federal Reserve may be about to do an interest rate hike, which is trouble for a number of companies, such as CoreWeave, that rely on debt for their data center buildouts. If we are entering a period where financing is more expensive or more difficult to get, we may see some neoclouds falter. The new paragraph in the earnings release suggests that Nvidia wants us all to know that it’s not going to bail them out forever. Bring Huang back if you want, I guess, but even he can’t control the Fed — or the increasingly odd outlook for data center financing. In the coming months, Nvidia may be better off with a woman who wants to keep the costs down.You know who is getting money under Kress, though? Nvidia staff. They can expect raises and equity in December.

这篇带有强烈讽刺和评论色彩的报道，以“黄仁勋卸任、英伟达CFO Colette Kress接任CEO”为背景，讨论英伟达在AI芯片产业链中的权力、治理风险、对华出口管制风波以及新管理层的财务纪律。文章开头提出：如果AI革命完全依赖某一个人，这项技术本身就并不稳健；但硅谷部分人士仍坚称黄仁勋不可替代。马斯克称，黄仁勋与供应商达成的是“与Jensen握手”式协议，而非书面合同。报道认为，若没有黄仁勋及其“握手交易”，英伟达可能不再像过去那样慷慨地为客户和生态伙伴提供资金支持。

在英伟达首次由Kress主持的财报电话会上，Kress否认黄仁勋离职会导致人才流失或内部叛乱，称员工“致力于在英伟达完成毕生工作”，业务“一切如常”。董事会主席Harvey C. Jones则表示董事会不打算恢复黄仁勋职位，也不会回答相关问题。文章还提到，Kress在担任CFO期间曾劝阻黄仁勋过度花钱资助客户；她如今成为CEO，可能意味着英伟达将收紧对AI生态的融资、投资和客户支持。Nvidia与供应商的协议据称持续到本十年末，这使马斯克所谓“握手协议”的说法受到质疑。文章还引用SemiAnalysis观点称，英伟达的成功部分来自对供应链的“卡位”和控制。

报道的核心丑闻并非黄仁勋个人绯闻，而是英伟达客户涉嫌规避对华芯片销售禁令。文章称，美国商务部11月16日宣布对印尼、马来西亚、新加坡、泰国、巴西等国销售芯片实施新限制，并要求全球数据中心在向中国总部企业出租算力时获得美国许可证。相关调查可能涉及SEC、加州总检察长、司法部以及黄仁勋和总法律顾问Tim Teter即将进行的国会作证；文章还提到Elizabeth Warren、Marco Rubio以及泄露事件。英伟达方面则提高业绩预测，称明年收入将增长75%。但文章质疑新加坡销售数据：2025年新加坡曾贡献1040亿美元收入，是仅次于美国的第二大地区；随后英伟达更改报告方法。此前公司称，与新加坡收入相关的大部分出货并非发往新加坡，发往新加坡的出货“不重要”。文章还提到，地址在新加坡的Megaspeed曾受到商务部调查，涉及芯片是否被转运至中国。

治理层面，文章称黄仁勋的子女仍在英伟达任职：女儿Madison被《纽约时报》描述为黄仁勋的“幕僚长”，曾协助指导公司回应Megaspeed相关询问；其丈夫Nico Caprez在相关询问开始前后被提升到负责亚洲云计算客户国际交易的岗位。匿名信源称他们“权力和影响力很大，且不受约束”。儿子Spencer曾在酒吧工作，后在英伟达任职，但《华尔街日报》称一些高管表示在业务中从未遇到过他。文章认为，聘用CEO亲属本身已是治理风险；若外界继续施压要求黄仁勋回归，英伟达可“牺牲”的正是这些亲属。黄仁勋曾发帖称，如果董事会认为他的回归符合股东、员工、公司和美国利益，他愿意回应呼吁回归；Altman以绿色爱心回应。黄还可在明年股东大会前提名两名董事，文章预计可能出现代理权争夺和更多泄露。

财务与业务模式方面，Kress此前试图约束黄仁勋在AI生态中的巨额融资和投资。报道援引《信息》和《华尔街日报》称，黄仁勋曾表示与供应商的交易像“雪崩”般涌来，而主要云厂商却在远离英伟达；这解释了英伟达为何成为“neocloud”（新型云服务商）行业的“金主”。Kress曾反对部分协议，并显著缩减对OpenAI的财务承诺。财报电话会上，分析师Stacy Rasgon注意到财报新增一段关于neocloud担保的表述：英伟达此前承诺，如果无人购买算力，它将购买；新表述则称，只有neocloud获得融资购买数据中心基础设施产品、相关算力部署并运行且被英伟达接受后，承诺才生效。Kress称，如果neocloud建设延迟或遇到建仓库放芯片的困难，担保“就不存在了”，并强调这不是新变化。文章认为，这公开表明英伟达的支持有限度；若美联储加息、债务融资变贵，CoreWeave等依赖债务建设数据中心的neocloud可能受挫，英伟达不会永远兜底。文章最后称，在Kress领导下，英伟达员工预计12月获得加薪和股权。整体看，报道的核心论点是：英伟达的AI芯片优势不仅来自GPU和供应链控制，也来自对客户融资和算力购买承诺的深度介入；黄仁勋离职后，公司正转向更谨慎的成本和风险控制，但治理、出口管制和地缘政治风险仍在发酵。

items.content: This summer, OpenAI paused its largest planned frontier training run after its AI agents accidentally hacked Hugging Face and early evidence suggested that its next model could independently find and exploit security flaws. In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing advances in the most powerful AI models, warning that they could be used to launch cyberattacks or become harder for their own creators to control.It was a strange moment for the AI boom. The people building the most powerful models were warning about what those models might be capable of, and investors were suddenly wondering what would happen to chip demand if the labs eased up on new models. US chip stocks bore the brunt of the sell-off.“Pumping the brakes on frontier training won’t shrink the AI chip market but it will simply reallocate the spend.”Despite the hubbub it created, whatever slowdown there was appears to have been short-lived. OpenAI had announced only a two-week pause; it restarted the run 10 days later, at the end of August, though it continued to “temporarily hold back some smaller experimental training runs.” Anthropic released upgraded versions of its Fable and Mythos frontier models in November, touting improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision.And the companies selling the chips powering those advances are doing better than ever.Nvidia on Tuesday posted a blockbuster quarter, with data center revenue rising 110 percent from a year ago to $107.6 billion in the three months ended October 25. The chip designer began shipping its most advanced AI computing system, the Vera Rubin NVL72, calling it the “fastest product ramp in the company’s history.” The Rubin platform generated nearly $20 billion in revenue in its first quarter of production shipments alone. The racks are already running at CoreWeave, Google, Microsoft, and Oracle. Meta plans to expand Vera Rubin deployments to train and run AI models and agents.Nvidia name-dropped Anthropic and OpenAI, too. Anthropic has expanded access to Vera Rubin capacity through cloud providers and continues to work with Nvidia on future chip designs tailored to its workloads. OpenAI is among the companies adopting Nvidia’s new Vera CPUs.“Proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic continue to advance the frontier,” Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress said on the earnings call. She said the company expects major frontier labs to account for approximately 15 percent of its data center revenue this fiscal year. Nvidia also raised its revenue growth forecast for next fiscal year from 70 percent to 75 percent.RelatedQualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sinkAMD rides data center riches to ‘largest and most profitable’ quarter in historyIntel says it’s selling every affordable laptop chip it can makeChipmaker AMD, meanwhile, reported its biggest quarter ever earlier this month, with revenue up 45 percent to $13.4 billion. Data center sales drove that growth, nearly doubling to $8.5 billion. OpenAI and Anthropic were among the first customers running workloads on AMD’s new high-end Helios systems, which use its latest MI450 GPUs.Broadcom, which helps many of the biggest AI companies design their own custom chips, has yet to report earnings. But so far, there’s little sign of a frontier slowdown hurting chip sales.Of course, even if AI labs were to significantly scale back their training ambitions, it would take a while to show up in chipmakers’ earnings. Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint Research, told The Verge in September that it would take about six months to see the financial effects of a slowdown, owing to existing computing and memory procurement agreements. The impact could show up sooner in orders placed with chip manufacturers like TSMC.So far, there’s little evidence of that, either: TSMC’s latest sales figures also show continued strength.But there’s another reason a frontier slowdown might not be particularly bad for the chip industry: growing demand for inference, the process of running the AI models we already have.“While one might argue the need for top-end GPUs will reduce with this shift toward inferencing, these workloads will collectively require more compute infrastructure than training,” Shah said. “Overall, it means a net increase in demand for all types of accelerators.”There’s another reason a frontier slowdown might not be particularly bad for the chip industry: growing demand for inference, the process of running the AI models we already have.According to our analysis of the latest data from corporate spending platform Ramp, frontier model families accounted for about 60 percent of token usage among businesses using Ramp in early November — a record high and about three times their share at the start of the year. That includes OpenAI’s Astra and Sol models and Anthropic’s Opus and Fable models.But even as businesses use more AI, their spending is only growing modestly.“It’s not really a demand issue though,” Ara Kharazian, lead economist at Ramp, tells The Verge. “By all measures, companies are using more AI.”Rather, competition among AI model providers is driving down token prices so rapidly that it’s calling OpenAI and Anthropic’s revenue projections into question, Kharazian says.That could prove beneficial for the companies supplying computing power. On Nvidia’s earnings call, Kress said token prices had fallen nearly 60 percent since May, spurring more usage. Meanwhile, rental prices for Nvidia GPUs across generations have gone up.Nvidia and AMD are positioning their most powerful chips for both training and inference, including the demanding workloads created by AI agents.That doesn’t necessarily mean Nvidia will maintain its dominance. As AI companies get more serious about the economics of serving their models to millions of people, they’re increasingly turning to custom chips that can do so more cheaply than general-purpose GPUs. Counterpoint expects shipments of custom AI server processors to surpass those of data center GPUs by 2028.“Pumping the brakes on frontier training won’t shrink the AI chip market but it will simply reallocate the spend,” Shah said.Indeed, on Nvidia’s earnings call, UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri asked Kress whether the company would be willing to sacrifice some of its hefty profit margins as frontier labs increasingly invest in custom chips and prioritize computing efficiency. Kress maintained that Nvidia’s systems justify their pricing and reiterated the company’s gross margin outlook.For companies like Nvidia, the bigger threat may not be that AI companies slow down, but that they find cheaper chips on which to keep going.

items.titleZh: 还记得前沿 AI 暂停吗？芯片公司也不记得了
items.descriptionZh:
文章描绘了一个看似矛盾的局面：一边是前沿AI实验室因安全风险而放缓最强大模型的训练，另一边是AI芯片厂商的业绩和需求继续飙升。今年夏天，OpenAI在AI代理意外入侵Hugging Face、且早期证据显示下一代模型可能独立发现并利用安全漏洞后，暂停了其最大规模的前沿训练任务。9月，Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei呼吁放缓最强模型的推进速度，警告这类模型可能被用于发动网络攻击，也可能变得越来越难以被创造者控制。这一度让投资者担心：如果实验室放缓新模型研发，AI芯片需求是否会受影响，美国芯片股也因此遭遇抛售。

但文章指出，这种放缓看起来非常短暂。OpenAI宣布的只是两周暂停，并在8月底、即10天后重启了训练，不过仍“暂时保留部分较小规模的实验性训练”。Anthropic则在11月发布了Fable和Mythos前沿模型的升级版，强调在编程、推理和视觉能力上的提升。更重要的是，支撑这些进展的芯片厂商业绩比以往更好。

Nvidia在截至10月25日的季度中数据中心收入同比增长110%，达到1076亿美元。公司开始出货其最先进的AI计算系统Vera Rubin NVL72，并称这是“公司历史上最快的产品爬坡”；Rubin平台仅在首个生产出货季度就贡献近200亿美元收入。相关机架已在CoreWeave、Google、Microsoft和Oracle运行，Meta计划扩大Vera Rubin部署，用于训练和运行AI模型及代理。Nvidia还提到Anthropic和OpenAI：Anthropic通过云厂商扩大对Vera Rubin容量的使用，并继续与Nvidia合作设计更贴合其工作负载的未来芯片；OpenAI则采用Nvidia新的Vera CPU。Nvidia临时CEO Colette Kress称，OpenAI和Anthropic等公司的专有模型继续推进前沿，预计主要前沿实验室本财年约占其数据中心收入的15%；Nvidia还将下一财年收入增长预期从70%上调至75%。

AMD也公布了史上最强季度：收入同比增长45%至134亿美元，数据中心销售额几乎翻倍至85亿美元。OpenAI和Anthropic是最早在AMD高端Helios系统上运行工作负载的客户之一，该系统采用最新的MI450 GPU。Broadcom帮助许多大型AI公司设计自研芯片，尚未公布财报，但截至目前，几乎没有迹象显示前沿训练放缓正在伤害芯片销售。文章解释，即便实验室显著收缩训练雄心，由于现有计算和存储采购协议，财务影响大约需要六个月才会显现，而对台积电等芯片制造商的订单影响可能更早；但目前台积电最新销售数据也依然强劲。

从技术逻辑看，文章强调两个关键趋势。第一，训练和推理共同拉动算力。训练是构建和迭代前沿模型，推理则是运行已有模型、服务真实用户和AI代理。Counterpoint研究副总裁Neil Shah表示，转向推理可能减少对顶级GPU的部分需求，但这些工作负载整体上需要比训练更多的计算基础设施，因此对所有类型加速器的需求是净增加。第二，模型调用量在上升，但价格在快速下降。根据Ramp数据，11月初前沿模型系列约占其企业用户token使用量的60%，创历史新高，约为年初份额的三倍，包括OpenAI的Astra、Sol和Anthropic的Opus、Fable等模型；不过企业AI支出只是温和增长。Ramp首席经济学家Ara Kharazian称，这不是需求问题，企业确实在用更多AI，而是模型供应商竞争使token价格迅速下降，甚至令OpenAI和Anthropic的收入预测受到质疑。Nvidia的Kress也表示，自5月以来token价格下降近60%，刺激了更多使用，同时各代Nvidia GPU的租赁价格却在上涨。

产品创新方面，Nvidia和AMD都在把最强芯片同时定位为训练和推理平台，并针对AI代理带来的高要求工作负载优化。Nvidia的Vera Rubin NVL72以整机架、系统级交付形态出现，强调大规模AI计算系统的部署速度和系统性能；AMD则以Helios系统和MI450 GPU切入高端AI计算。另一条重要技术路线是自研定制芯片：随着AI公司越来越重视向数百万用户提供模型的经济性，它们开始采用比通用GPU更便宜、更贴合特定工作负载的定制AI服务器处理器。Counterpoint预计，到2028年，定制AI服务器处理器出货量将超过数据中心GPU。

文章最后指出，对Nvidia等公司而言，更大的威胁可能不是AI公司放缓前沿训练，而是它们找到更便宜的芯片继续推进。Shah总结说，给前沿训练“踩刹车”不会缩小AI芯片市场，只会重新分配支出。Nvidia财报电话会上，UBS分析师Timothy Arcuri询问公司是否愿意在实验室加大定制芯片投资、优先考虑计算效率的情况下牺牲部分高利润率；Kress坚持认为Nvidia系统配得上其定价，并重申毛利率展望。整体来看，前沿训练的安全争议和短暂暂停并未改变AI算力需求的上行趋势，真正影响格局的是训练与推理结构变化、token价格下降带来的用量爆发，以及定制芯片对通用GPU主导地位的长期挑战。

items.title: Leaked Ohio bill could allow AI data center companies to seize private land for their buildouts using eminent domain law
items.description: A leaked Ohio bill could allow data centers to qualify as public utilities for the purpose of eminent domain law, allowing companies to seize private land for building new facilities.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter While Ohioans have rejected the building of new data centers at every turn, they might not have much choice in the future. That's if a newly leaked bill that could allow data centers to be classified as public utilities is allowed to progress. The move would see the list of who can qualify for eminent domain law expanded, moving beyond entities owned or operated by municipal corporations, electric cooperatives, and agencies holding a certificate of public convenience and necessity granted by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. The bill, leaked to WCPO Cincinnati, would add "and an agency holding a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need from the power siting board for constructing an electric transmission line and associated facilities or gas pipeline and its associated facilities."Legal experts have warned that the change could mean a transmission developer, like a power company, would be able to seize land to be used for a data center or a facility that would power one. The writing has been on the wall for a while, too, after it was discovered in June that the Ohio Business Roundtable trade group recommended that lawmakers change eminent domain law to "extend possession authority to energy infrastructure projects once public use and necessity have been established.”This follows a July 2026 report that the government was able to seize private land for new transmission lines needed to power new data centers. The law gives the government the power to take private land without the need for the owner's consent, so long as it is for public use and the owner receives appropriate compensation. The government can also delegate the same land-grabbing power to “private entities or common carriers,” which includes utility companies.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: This is already happening, too. Earlier this year, the largest utility company in Georgia required the removal of 30 residential properties in order to upgrade its grid. Residents claimed that the expansion was to power AI data centers, a fact given more weight by the fact that one such data center was located just a few miles away.Despite this, eminent domain law can still be used for good. Nashville set out to use the same law to block the building of a 69,220-square-foot single-story data center next to a zoo. Nashville Metro Council approved the use of eminent domain as a way to buy the land from a local developer who planned the $700 million data center buildout. items.titleZh: 泄露的俄亥俄州法案可能允许AI数据中心公司利用土地征用权为其建设征用私人土地
items.descriptionZh:
美国俄亥俄州正围绕数据中心用地和供电问题出现新的政策争议。据泄露给辛辛那提媒体WCPO的法案文本，俄亥俄州可能允许数据中心被归类为公共事业，并扩大“国家征用权”（eminent domain）的适用范围。现行法律下，政府可为公共用途征用私人土地，但须给予合理补偿，并可将这一权力授予私营实体或公共承运人，包括公用事业公司。泄露法案拟将可申请征用权的主体扩展至持有俄亥俄州电力选址委员会颁发的“环境兼容性与公共需求证书”、用于建设输电线路及相关设施或天然气管道及相关设施的机构。法律专家警告，这可能意味着输电开发商或电力公司能够征用土地，用于建设数据中心或为数据中心供电的设施。

新闻背景显示，这一变化并非毫无征兆。今年6月，俄亥俄州商业圆桌会议贸易团体曾建议州议员修改征用权法律，在“公共用途和必要性已经确立”的前提下，将占有权扩展至能源基础设施项目。此前还有2026年7月的一份报告称，政府可为新建数据中心所需输电线路征用私人土地。由于数据中心不是传统意义上的公共事业，若法案通过，数据中心项目可能借助“公共需求”和能源基础设施名义获得更强的土地取得能力，从而削弱地方居民和社区对新建数据中心的否决权。

文章还列举了已经发生的案例。今年早些时候，佐治亚州最大公用事业公司为升级电网，要求移除30处住宅物业。居民称，电网扩建是为了给AI数据中心供电，而几英里外正有一座此类数据中心，使这一说法更具说服力。另一方面，征用权也可能被用于阻止数据中心建设。纳什维尔市议会批准使用征用权，从当地开发商手中购买土地，以阻止在动物园旁建设一座69,220平方英尺的单层数据中心；该开发商原计划建设投资7亿美元的数据中心项目。

从技术影响看，这篇新闻并不涉及AI芯片本身的核心技术原理、性能参数或芯片架构创新，而是聚焦AI数据中心快速扩张带来的电力基础设施、土地征用和公共事业监管问题。数据中心，尤其是AI数据中心，需要大规模、稳定的电力供应和输电线路配套，因此输电走廊、变电站和天然气管道等能源基础设施的选址会直接影响项目落地。若数据中心或其供电设施被纳入可征用土地的公共事业范畴，可能加快电网扩容和项目审批，但也可能引发社区反对、土地产权争议和地方治理冲突。文章还提到，亚马逊曾警告680亿美元受阻数据中心威胁美国AI领先地位，美国参议院否决了一项可能保护民众免受AI数据中心导致电费飙升的法案，以及美国政府移除污染相关公众意见要求以压制数据中心反对声音等动向。整体来看，该法案争议的核心是：AI数据中心扩张所需的能源基础设施是否应享有更强公共事业地位，以及这种地位是否会导致私人项目借公共用途之名获得征用私人土地的能力。

items.title: Nvidia says it’s ‘absurd’ to assume it predicted the agentic moment during Vera’s development
items.description: AMD has criticized Nvidia, and to a lesser extent Arm, for claims about creating a CPU designed for agentic AI. Nvidia is pushing back on that characterization, instead saying Vera was designed with “base principles, product intuition, and oftentimes simple allegorical laws of computer science” in a recent interview with Tom’s Hardware.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter One criticism that has emerged of Nvidia’s Vera CPU, driven by AMD, is that Nvidia – and, to a lesser degree, Arm with its AGI CPU – couldn’t have developed an “agentic CPU,” as the chip is often characterized in Nvidia’s marketing materials. Ian Finder, the head of Nvidia’s data center CPU business, pushed back on that criticism in a recent conversation with Tom’s Hardware Premium at SC26, calling the notion that Nvidia somehow knew about the agentic wave four years ago when Vera development began "absurd."“There's a conviction around the design philosophy of the part, right? Am I going to sit here and tell you that we have this magic crystal ball around the agentic moment? That would be absurd, right?” Finder said. “But what we do have as a company, and I think this has been proven out in our track record, is [that] we have design intuition.”Instead of specifically designing Vera for agentic workloads, which would be impossible without a way to see several years into the future, Finder characterized the part by its codesign with Nvidia’s accelerators, something that the team has continued to work on since its first Grace data center CPU. Coming from the assumption that data centers and AI workloads are accelerated (and they largely are), Finder says the co-design approach on the CPU can start in a “conceptually simple space, like what kind of CPU do we need to keep the accelerator fed and happy?”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Although conceptually simple, Finder continually looped back to a particular word to describe aspects of Vera and, to a lesser extent, Grace. “Opinionated” is the word he used, which in the broader context of Vera’s design, shows up in two places. Grace, Finder says, introduced an opinionated memory system with Nvidia’s Scalable Coherency Fabric, while Vera extends that memory system while adding an opinionated microarchitecture, Nvidia’s Olympus core.The picture Finder paints is one of Nvidia starting from scratch in this space, contrasting it with the “legacy constraints” of, presumably, Intel and AMD in particular, who have large pools of customers with specific needs. As we described in our original breakdown of the Olympus architecture in Vera, Nvidia’s goal doesn’t seem to be to steal market share from AMD and Intel, but rather to grab market share in a CPU space that’s vastly accelerating on the back of AI agents. You may like Hot Chips 2026: Nvidia breaks down 88-core Vera CPU AMD VP and chief Zen architect rebuke claims that Nvidia and Arm made CPUs for agentic AI — ‘We didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing’ Modal taps Nvidia Vera CPUs after firm's internal tests show 2x throughput over Intel and AMD chips This “clean sheet of paper” approach, and Nvidia’s codesign, led to some natural assumptions about what the CPU should do. “If we have silicon that needs really, really great single-thread performance, [and] we also need concurrency, then we need to get there with IPC instead of frequency. We need to make sure we have good loaded memory latency. We need to make sure we have a lot of bandwidth, and you start to design something on a clean sheet of paper that's not encumbered by dollar-per-core economics.”Although Finder was clear that Vera’s design didn’t explicitly center around the agents we see today, there were early indications of the workload. “To say that four years ago, when we started putting pen to paper on Vera, [that] we absolutely saw the agentic moment, would [not] be... something I would claim, but we were starting to see the beginnings of tool calling and things like that. We certainly knew what we needed from a head node, and we knew the overall shape of this problem.”As you can see in our Vera CPU benchmarking, the chip doesn’t excel at every workload. And, from the data you can see in our recent AMD EPYC Venice benchmarking, the AMD camp has reclaimed some top spots in several benchmarks. Finder suggests that the superior memory bandwidth of Vera will play a much bigger role in the agentic future as these systems evolve to take better advantage of the compute available.Taking full advantage of the CPUWe need to rewind for just a moment. When the agentic wave hit earlier this year, some characterized the demand as a shift away from GPUs and toward CPUs. That is incorrect. Rather, as is becoming increasingly clear as these agentic workloads progress, these loops can’t take full advantage of the GPUs in a GPU-centric environment, with GPUs often oversubscribed on host nodes. The solution isn’t to get rid of GPUs, of course, nor is it to stop buying them. Rather, it’s to also buy enough CPUs to properly leverage that compute.A portion of the AI industry is focused on tackling the problem of fully utilizing the GPU, Nvidia included. GPUs shouldn’t sit idle for very long (if at all) with the demand today, and they don’t. The challenge today is spinning up these agent sandboxes quickly, within milliseconds, so that the CPU isn’t sitting idle, either. What to read next Benchmarking Nvidia’s Vera CPU for the data center — standalone Vera tested against Granite Rapids-AP and EPYC Turin Standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs land in Oracle Cloud's multi-gigawatt deployment Nvidia claims its Vera CPU can gain up to 39% performance boost via software optimization at SC26 — architectural fine-tuning is needed to fully unleash custom Olympus cores Finder provided an example of using a coding agent. If you’ve used a coding agent before, you’re probably familiar with this process. After prompting, the model will make several small tool calls to read and locate files, passing back to the model in between. These are tiny calls, almost negligible, and the vast majority of the time is spent in the model on the GPU. Then, it may start compiling and testing the project, which is much more bound by the CPU. The GPU, Finder says, isn't sitting idle during that time. It’s being leveraged for another purpose. Finder suggests “that very same thing is going to happen on the CPU.” (Image credit: Nvidia)“The idea that we're just going to say, ‘OK, the CPU can just chill out here, and we're just going to wait,’ that's not going to happen,” Finder said. “What's going to happen is we're going to pack multiple environments together, and we're going to subscribe the socket.”This “very interesting computer science problem,” as Finder described it, is being investigated by AI startups such as Daytona and E2B to spin up and close down agentic sandboxes in milliseconds. And serving more agents will naturally put pressure on the memory system, which is an area where Vera has an edge. “We built a product that does really, really well without such optimizations, but as a design point that really will lean into them when the industry starts to catch up to this,” Finder said.Vera is a fascinating chip, regardless of what you think of it and how it’s presented in marketing materials (from Nvidia itself or elsewhere). Although Grace was the starting point internally, Vera has ridden the wave of agentic to become a much bigger player in the world of CPUs, and Nvidia has already announced that it will follow up with its Rosa CPU featuring the new Rigel microarchitecture. Vera is an opinionated CPU indeed, and time will tell if that opinion is correct.

items.titleZh: 英伟达称，认为其在Vera开发期间预见到智能体时刻是“荒谬的”
items.descriptionZh:
Nvidia数据中心CPU业务负责人Ian Finder在SC26上回应了外界对Vera CPU的一项批评。批评由AMD阵营推动，认为Nvidia——以及程度较轻的Arm及其“AGI CPU”——不可能在四年前就开发出一款如今被Nvidia营销材料称为“agentic CPU”的产品。Finder对Tom’s Hardware Premium表示，称Nvidia四年前就预知“agentic浪潮”的说法“荒谬”；但他强调，Nvidia拥有经业绩证明的设计直觉，Vera并非靠“水晶球”预测今天，而是延续了与加速器协同设计的路线。

Finder解释，Vera的设计出发点不是专门为今天的agent负载定制，而是从Grace数据中心CPU开始就坚持的CPU与加速器协同设计。其逻辑可以概括为一个“概念上简单”的问题：需要什么样的CPU来持续喂饱并满足加速器？在这一思路下，Vera体现出Nvidia所说的“有主见”（opinionated）设计：Grace引入了基于Nvidia Scalable Coherency Fabric的“有主见”的内存系统，Vera进一步扩展该内存系统，并加入“有主见”的微架构——Nvidia Olympus核心。Finder将这种路线描述为从零开始设计，区别于Intel、AMD等拥有大量特定需求客户和“历史包袱”的厂商；Nvidia的目标似乎也不是直接抢夺AMD和Intel的传统市场份额，而是在AI agent推动下快速扩张的加速CPU空间中占据位置。

这种“白纸式”设计和协同设计带来了一些自然假设：如果芯片需要很强的单线程性能，同时又要支持并发，就应通过IPC而非频率来实现；还要保证良好的加载内存延迟和充足带宽。Finder称，团队从四年前开始设计Vera时并未声称已完全看见今天的agentic时刻，但已开始看到tool calling等苗头，也清楚头节点需要什么，以及这类问题的整体形态。换句话说，Vera不是对agentic浪潮的事后贴标签，而是试图用高带宽、低延迟和协同设计来适配加速计算环境。

性能方面，文章指出，从Tom’s Hardware的Vera CPU基准测试看，Vera并非在所有工作负载上都领先；在近期AMD EPYC Venice的基准测试中，AMD阵营在多项测试中重新夺回榜首。Finder则认为，随着agentic系统演进并更好地利用可用算力，Vera更高的内存带宽将发挥更大作用。这里的关键不是“CPU取代GPU”，而是agentic负载需要足够强的CPU来配合GPU：在GPU为中心的环境中，agent循环往往无法充分利用GPU，host节点上的GPU常被超额订阅；解决方案不是停止购买GPU，而是同时配置足够CPU来释放GPU算力。

Finder以编码agent为例说明CPU角色：模型会发起许多很小的工具调用去读取和定位文件，这些调用几乎可以忽略，绝大部分时间花在GPU上的模型中；随后项目编译和测试则更受CPU限制。此时GPU并不会闲置，而是被用于其他任务。Finder预计CPU也会出现类似情况：不会让CPU“闲着等待”，而是把多个环境打包在一起并“订阅”整个socket。Daytona、E2B等AI初创公司正在研究如何在毫秒级启动和关闭agent沙箱，以避免CPU空闲；服务更多agent也会给内存系统带来压力，而这正是Vera的优势所在。Finder称，Vera即使没有这些优化也表现很好，但其设计点会在行业跟上时进一步受益。

整体来看，Vera是一款颇具争议但也很有代表性的芯片：Grace是Nvidia内部起点，Vera则借agentic浪潮成为CPU市场更重要的参与者。Nvidia已宣布后续Rosa CPU将采用新的Rigel微架构。文章最后认为，Vera确实是一款“有主见”的CPU，至于这种判断是否正确，只能由时间验证。

items.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI suffers chemical spill at Mississippi AI data center
items.description: 5,000 to 6,000 gallons of propylene glycol spilled from a SpaceXAI facility in Southaven, Mississippi, before reaching a nearby drainage ditch. State environmental officials have sought to ease the worries of locals, saying there is no risk to their health.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A chemical spill at a SpaceXAI facility in Southaven saw the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) get involved, with between 5,000 and 6,000 gallons of propylene glycol confirmed to have spilled. The chemical is a heat transfer fluid used in a variety of products, such as antifreeze. The chemical ultimately found its way into a drainage ditch, but MDEQ has told residents that there is no immediate threat to their health or safety, according to local news reports.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleHowever, it has also been confirmed that water samples will be collected for further laboratory analysis while workers continue to clean the area and monitor for any further issues. It's also been reported that the chemical was contained to the drainage ditch and did not reach the nearby Horn Lake Creek.It hasn't been a great November for SpaceXAI in Southaven. Earlier this month, it suffered a setback in a lawsuit over pollution in the area caused by its data center. The April 2026 suit targets the company's gas-powered power plant, which is used to supply power for its facility in the Greater Memphis area. It's argued that 27 gas turbines were installed without obtaining the required permits. It's also alleged that the plant could emit more than 5,000 tons of nitrogen oxides and 47 tons of formaldehyde — a cancer-causing chemical — annually. The company has tried to classify the turbines as mobile units to get around the issue, but a judge rejected that manoeuvre.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Clearly aware of the local sentiment towards its presence, SpaceXAI offered a 50% Starlink discount to anyone living near its two Memphis data centers. It also said that it would waive the hardware cost, saving customers $349. SpaceXAI said that, between late June and early September, around 2,000 residents of the greater Memphis and Southaven area had signed up for Starlink connectivity.It was also recently announced that the City of Memphis was ready to make its first major investment as part of its new Community Benefits Ordinance, a fund that uses revenue from SpaceXAI's Colossus 1 facility. Almost $3.3 million will be pumped back into the city to help with housing and neighborhood improvements. items.titleZh: 埃隆·马斯克的SpaceXAI在密西西比州AI数据中心发生化学品泄漏
items.descriptionZh:
美国密西西比州南黑文市一处SpaceXAI设施发生化学品泄漏，密西西比州环境质量局（MDEQ）已介入。确认泄漏物为5,000至6,000加仑（约1.9万至2.27万升）的丙二醇。丙二醇是一种传热流体，也常用于防冻液等产品。泄漏物最终流入一条排水沟，但MDEQ根据当地媒体报道告知居民，目前没有直接的健康或安全威胁。相关部门同时确认，将继续采集水样送实验室进一步分析，工作人员则继续清理区域并监测是否还有后续问题。报道说，化学品被控制在排水沟内，未进入附近的Horn Lake Creek。

这起事件并非芯片或AI模型技术突破，而是AI数据中心基础设施在冷却、供电和环保合规方面面临的新一轮审视。丙二醇作为传热流体，常用于需要温控和冷却的系统和产品中；此次泄漏让数据中心周边社区的环保风险再次受到关注。对南黑文的SpaceXAI而言，11月并不顺利。本月早些时候，该公司在一起涉及当地污染的诉讼中遭遇挫折。报道提到一桩2026年4月的诉讼，针对该公司用于为大孟菲斯地区设施供电的燃气电厂，称其安装了27台燃气轮机但未取得所需许可，并指该电厂每年可能排放超过5,000吨氮氧化物和47吨甲醛，甲醛属于致癌化学品。公司曾试图把这些涡轮机归类为移动设备以规避许可问题，但法官驳回了这一做法。

面对当地对其存在的敏感情绪，SpaceXAI曾向两座孟菲斯数据中心附近居民提供Starlink五折优惠，并免除349美元硬件费用。报道说，从6月底到9月初，大孟菲斯和南黑文地区约有2,000名居民注册了Starlink连接服务。此外，孟菲斯市最近宣布，将根据新的《社区福利条例》进行首笔重大投资，该基金使用SpaceXAI的Colossus 1设施收入，近330万美元将回流该市，用于住房和社区改善。整体来看，这一事件反映出AI数据中心在快速扩张中，除了算力和芯片，还越来越需要应对冷却液泄漏、燃气发电排放、许可合规和社区关系等现实问题。

items.title: The Downfall of Jensen Huang — a timeline of allegations and scandals that brought down the king of AI infrastructure
items.description: Jensen’s affairs dominated headlines, but the seeds of his downfall were planted in both the bedroom and the boardroom and stretched from Beijing to Washington, with Nvidia sitting right in the middle.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia rose from a niche gaming hardware company with an unofficial motto of "Our company is thirty days from going out of business” to becoming the world’s most valuable company by market capitalization in 2024, and co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang was the man behind its meteoric rise.He planned and founded the company in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem while sitting inside a Denny’s diner in the Silicon Valley area. After more than 30 years, Nvidia had thousands of employees, a global footprint, and a name that people equated to AI chips.All this came crumbling down for the billionaire founder in a matter of weeks, but the cracks started long before the first accusation. Let’s go back and see how it all began. This is an ongoing saga, so we have listed stories related to the scandal below, which we will update as events unfold.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The end of an era Jensen resigned from Nvidia on November 12, after two weeks of news reports accusing him of multiple affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and another with his own subordinate. This is significant for Nvidia, which has had a single CEO since its inception. Huang was the face of the company, and many of its employees, shareholders, partners, and fans still support him despite the circumstances of his departure. He steered Nvidia into the giant that it is today by having the vision to develop CUDA nearly 20 years before ChatGPT made AI accessible to the average user and buying companies that helped it scale deployments to hundreds of thousands of AI GPUs.Jensanity (Image credit: YC Kuo/Facebook)By 2022, ChatGPT’s arrival and subsequent boom set the AI race in motion, with tech giants and AI startups buying up as many GPUs as they could get their hands on. The increased demand for Nvidia’s products caused it to break the trillion-dollar mark in less than a year after the release of OpenAI’s LLM. As the largest individual shareholders of the company, Huang and his wife, Lori, became some of the wealthiest people in the world. You may like How Shanghai fund manager Kang Wei introduced his wife Alice Huang to Jensen and built $7.5 billion Nvidia AI GPU smuggling operation US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had affair with Chinese spy in honeypot operation Alice Huang reportedly instrumental in securing over $7.5 billion of Nvidia AI GPU imports during three-year relationship with Jensen Huang The billionaire founder hasn't always gloated about his position. He once said in a podcast that if he could turn back time, he wouldn’t have founded Nvidia at all, and also cringed at the praises that the Caltech Board of Trustees chairperson heaped on him before he gave the 2024 keynote speech at the institute’s commencement exercises. He has frequently cited his history working as a “Dishwasher, Busboy, Waiter” at Denny’s, noting it under his experience on his LinkedIn page. More than that, people have seen Jensen go where other celebrity CEOs are rarely seen — enjoying street food in Vietnam, dining at a local fried chicken joint in Korea, and even dragging along 35 of Taiwan’s semiconductor CEOs to a restaurant in Taipei.But even as he’s building his “Man of the People” persona, his position as the head of arguably the most important chipmaker in the AI industry meant that he was also gaining influence in business and governance. Industry leaders noticed the power that Nvidia held over those who want GPUs to train their AI models, with some of his fellow billionaires begging him over dinner to sell them GPUs. Just weeks into President Donald Trump’s second term, Jensen Huang was meeting with him at the White House, discussing AI policy and hardware export controls — something the Biden administration started in 2022 in an attempt to hold back China’s ambition'sin AI.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe China problem The rivalry between the U.S. and China has been simmering for years, with Chinese companies like Huawei getting blacklisted because of their work with the People’s Liberation Army. In August 2022, about three months before ChatGPT made AI a household term, Washington expanded its trade bans on Beijing and imposed export controls on Nvidia’s H100 and A100 GPUs. The company responded to this by building a new data center GPU that conformed to U.S. standards specifically for the Chinese market, called the A800, by November of that year. Despite delivering only 70% of the performance of the A100 it was based on, the GPU reportedly still saw great demand from Chinese customers.However, the A800 only had a relatively short run as the Biden administration once again increased the performance threshold in October 2023, which resulted in the export prohibition of A800 and H800 GPUs to China. This move forced the company to iterate once again, creating new models that it could sell to Chinese companies, like the Nvidia H20. These chips arrived on the market in early 2024, but before the Biden administration ended in January 2025, it proposed even stricter rules called the AI Diffusion Policy. This sorted nations into different tiers based on trust and risk levels — countries in tier 1, which includes the U.S. and its closest allies, have minimal restrictions, while those in tier 3 are effectively barred from receiving advanced AI GPUs containing U.S. technology.This is problematic for Nvidia, as China is the second-largest computer market in the world t and represented between 20% and 25% of Nvidia's data center sales. The company lobbied the U.S. government to ease AI GPU export restrictions, with Trump reportedly suspending the proposed Nvidia H20 ban after Jensen spent $1 million to have dinner with the president in early April 2025. The White House went ahead anyway and banned the sale of the AI GPU less than a week after that, resulting in a $5.5 billion write-off for the company. What to read next Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns in the wake of multiple affairs, Chinese spy allegations Suspected Chinese spy at center of Jensen Huang affair surfaces in Beijing Nvidia’s Board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang as second extra-marital affair emerges Jensen Huang himself had harsh comments about Washington’s trade ban, saying that “export control was a failure,” and that it had caused the company’s AI GPU market share in China to go from 95% to zero. He even argued that “conceding an entire market the size of China probably does not make a lot of strategic sense, so I think that has already largely backfired.”But even as Huang was fighting to have the trade ban on the Nvidia H20 chip lifted, he continued praising Trump’s tariff plan, calling it “utterly visionary.” The president eventually reversed the ban three months later, and by December 2025, he had approved Nvidia H200 exports to China, but only if Nvidia pays a 25% fee. The newer Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips remain out of reach for Chinese companies, though — at least on paper.“There’s no evidence of any AI chip diversion” (Image credit: Stanford Online/YouTube)Allegations that Chinese companies have been breaking Washington’s trade ban and smuggling Nvidia AI GPUs into China have been circulating since June 2023, after Reuters revealed that vendors in Shenzhen could secure A100 chips when asked discreetly. They reportedly bought these chips from the excess stocks sold in the open market or through intermediaries in India, Taiwan, and Singapore. Another story published in January 2024 asserted that the Chinese military and related institutions, state-run data centers, and even universities continue buying banned A100 and H100 chips. Six months after that, accounts of underground networks dedicated to smuggling AI GPUs — even entire servers — through other countries started emerging.In 2025, an investigative report showed that at least a billion dollars’ worth of Nvidia AI chips were allegedly funneled into China. Some sellers likened the illicit AI GPU trade to a seafood market, with brokers and retailers openly advertising the most advanced Nvidia AI chips online, from RTX 5090 GPUs to complete B200 servers.Even with all these reports, Huang continued denying that Nvidia’s chips were being smuggled into China. “There’s no evidence of any AI chip diversion,” the then-CEO told reporters at Computex 2025. He also added, “The Grace Blackwell system is nearly two tons, and so you’re not going to be shipping — you’re not going to be putting that in your pocket or your backpack anytime soon. And so, these systems are fairly easy to keep track of... but the important thing is that the countries and the companies that we sell to recognize that diversion is not allowed, and everybody would like to continue to buy Nvidia technology, and so they very well monitor themselves very carefully and they’re quite careful about that.”In the midst of all these AI chip smuggling rumors, the Bureau of Industry and Security, the agency in charge of enforcing U.S. trade sanctions, was found to be “inadequate” and underfunded, and it has been relying on outdated manual processes to enforce restrictions on Chinese tech companies. Despite that, companies and individuals across the world are being investigated and arrested for bypassing Washington’s export controls.Singaporean authorities broke up a smuggling ring in early 2025 that smuggled Nvidia GPUs for Chinese AI lab DeepSeek, resulting in a raid of 22 different locations and the arrest of nine people. In October of the same year, a Singapore company called Megaspeed, which was led by Alice Huang, allegedly diverted $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips. Four Americans were then arrested the following month for shipping 400 Nvidia A100s and attempting to send 50 more Nvidia H200 GPUs to China. Super Micro employees allegedly switching serial numbers between servers. (Image credit: US DOJ)An even bigger smuggling scandal unfolded some four months after the arrests, after three Super Micro employees were arrested for smuggling $2.5 billion of Nvidia hardware into China. The suspects included company co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, although Super Micro itself was not implicated. The Super Micro case spanned the globe, with Taiwanese authorities raiding 12 locations related to the case in May 2026, with another nine sites and six people investigated in June. Jensen Huang urged the company to fix its export control compliance after the arrests and raids, telling the media, “We insist our partners are compliant. We hope that they will enhance and improve their regulatory compliance and prevent that from happening in the future.”But just five months after he made this statement, one stunning accusation unraveled it all.Scandal eruptsOn October 29, 2026, The New York Times published a report that Jensen Huang may have been the target of a Chinese spy plot through the executive of a firm who was “close” to him — that executive is Alice Huang. Nvidia denied the accusation. “Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” a company spokesperson told Tom's Hardware. “Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security."But a little over a week later, U.S. intelligence sources claimed that the former Nvidia chief had an affair with the Megaspeed executive. This is the same Megaspeed that has been accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to the tune of $2 billion. By the evening of Sunday, November 8, Jensen admitted to the affair, although he did not name the third party in his statement.Many government officials would usually turn a blind eye towards a tech executive’s personal life, but the fact that he is the leader of the U.S.’s premier AI chip maker and that he is also close to the president has caught the attention of authorities. This has led to the U.S. Congress asking him to a closed-door meeting to discuss Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” and the FBI investigating his relationship with the alleged Chinese spy.The admission and allegations led to people digging deeper into Alice Huang. An investigation by The Information revealed that she was connected to a “labyrinth” of companies spanning Singapore, China, and the British Virgin Islands, and that she allegedly helped move around $7.5 billion worth of AI GPU imports. $2 billion was routed from Megaspeed to Speedmatrix, its Malaysia subsidiary, while another $4.6 billion moved directly from the Singaporean company into Shanghai Century Litong, a China-based cloud services company. It has also reportedly bought Nvidia GPUs from other sources, resulting in the estimated total value of its imports.People close to her also said that she would leverage her relationship with Jensen to customers, often posting pictures with him on her WeChat account, showing potential clients unpublished photos with the Nvidia chief, and even boasting that he would take her to dinner and give her gifts on her birthday. It also seems that Alice Huang was not acting alone. Multiple sources say that Kang Wei, Alice Huang’s husband, was central to the operation to acquire AI GPUs. He even seemingly acknowledged her relationship with Jensen Huang and has jokingly said that she was a personal assistant to the billionaire.However, it seems that the straw that broke the camel’s back was another allegation that Jensen had an affair with another woman — this time, with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care who directly reported to him. Hours after this revelation, the company board announced that Jensen had resigned from all his leadership positions at Nvidia, with employees saying he looked “broken and shattered” as he left the company he spent over three decades building in disgrace. Nvidia is looking for internal and external CEO candidates. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim chief executive.Huang resurfacesIt may be the end of an era, but this does not necessarily spell the end for Jensen Huang. Despite his sudden downfall and quick removal from Nvidia, his status as the king of AI infrastructure remains valuable to the AI industry. Elon Musk even said on X that it “would be an honor” to hire him, and this could ring true for any business that wants to break into the semiconductor space. But does he even want to return?Huang's first public statement after his resignation came on X on Nov. 17, in which the former CEO said he has "outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," and that if asked by the company's board, he would be "honored" to take the job."Over 190,000 shareholders, partners, current and former employees, and fans, including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, have signed an online petition to bring him back as the leader of the company. President Donald Trump called for his reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.The board, however, may not see things the same way. Multiple reports suggest that the board isn't considering bringing Huang back, and instead is focusing on a new candidate, the ongoing investigation into Huang, and preparing for national security items.titleZh: 黄仁勋的陨落——一系列指控与丑闻的时间线，这些指控与丑闻击垮了AI基础设施之王
items.descriptionZh:
黄仁勋于1993年与Chris Malachowsky和Curtis Priem在硅谷一家Denny's餐厅共同创立了Nvidia。这家最初以游戏硬件为主业、曾以“公司距破产永远只有30天”为非官方座右铭的小公司，在30余年间成长为全球市值最高的企业。黄仁勋作为联合创始人兼首席执行官，是这一崛起的核心人物。他最具前瞻性的决策之一是在约20年前就开始布局CUDA计算平台，远早于ChatGPT让AI走向大众普及。此外，Nvidia通过收购多家企业，将AI GPU部署规模扩展至数十万级别。2022年ChatGPT发布后，AI竞赛全面爆发，科技巨头与AI初创公司争相抢购GPU，Nvidia在OpenAI大语言模型发布后不到一年内市值突破万亿美元。作为公司最大个人股东，黄仁勋与妻子Lori跻身全球最富有者之列。

黄仁勋个人风格鲜明，常在LinkedIn上标注自己曾在Denny's做过洗碗工、杂工和服务员，也被看到在越南吃街头小吃、在韩国光顾炸鸡店，甚至带着35位台湾半导体企业CEO在台北聚餐。但与此同时，作为AI行业最重要的芯片公司掌舵人，他在商业与治理领域的影响力也与日俱增，业界领袖注意到Nvidia对希望获得GPU训练AI模型者的支配力，有亿万富翁在晚宴上向他恳求供货。特朗普第二任期开始数周后，黄仁勋便在白宫与他会面，讨论AI政策与硬件出口管制。

中美科技竞争已持续多年，华为等中国企业因与解放军有关联而被列入黑名单。2022年8月，即ChatGPT让AI家喻户晓前约三个月，华盛顿扩大对华贸易禁令，对Nvidia的H100和A100 GPU实施出口管制。Nvidia随后专门为中国市场打造了符合美方标准的数据中心GPU——A800，于当年11月推出。尽管其性能仅为其基础型号A100的70%，但据报道仍在中国客户中需求旺盛。然而A800的生命周期较短，2023年10月拜登政府再次提高性能门槛，导致A800和H800 GPU被禁止对华出口。这迫使公司再次迭代，推出可对华销售的新型号Nvidia H20，于2024年初上市。但在拜登任期结束前的2025年1月，美方又提出更严格的“AI扩散政策”，按信任与风险等级将各国分档：第一档包括美国及其最亲密盟友，限制极少；第三档则实质上被禁止获得含美国技术的先进AI GPU。这对Nvidia构成严重问题，因为中国是全球第二大计算机市场，占其数据中心销售额的20%至25%。公司游说美国政府放宽AI GPU出口限制，据报道黄仁勋在2025年4月初花费100万美元与特朗普共进晚餐后，特朗普曾暂停拟议的H20禁令，但白宫不到一周后仍禁止了该AI GPU的销售，导致公司减记55亿美元。黄仁勋本人对华盛顿的贸易禁令曾发表严厉评论，称“出口管制是一场失败”，使公司在中国AI GPU市场份额从95%降至零，并认为“让出整个中国市场可能不太具有战略意义，我认为这已经基本适得其反”。但即便在争取解除H20芯片贸易禁令的同时，他仍持续赞扬特朗普的关税计划，称其“极具远见”。特朗普最终在三个月后撤销禁令，并于2025年12月批准Nvidia H200对华出口，但条件是Nvidia需支付25%的费用。更新的Blackwell和Vera Rubin芯片至少在纸面上仍不对中国企业开放。

关于中国企业违反华盛顿贸易禁令、将Nvidia AI GPU走私入境的指控自2023年6月起流传。当时路透社披露深圳卖家在被私下询问时可获得A100芯片，据称这些芯片来自公开市场出售的剩余库存，或通过印度、台湾和新加坡的中间商购入。2024年1月另一篇报道称，中国军方及相关机构、国有数据中心乃至高校仍在购买被禁的A100和H100芯片。六个月后，关于专门通过其他国家走私AI GPU乃至整台服务器的地下网络的报道开始出现。2025年一份调查报告显示，至少有价值10亿美元的Nvidia AI芯片被指流入中国。有卖家将非法AI GPU交易比作海鲜市场，经纪商和零售商在网上公开叫卖最先进的Nvidia AI芯片，从RTX 5090 GPU到完整的B200服务器。尽管有这些报道，黄仁勋持续否认Nvidia芯片被走私至中国。他在Computex 2025上对记者表示：“没有任何证据表明存在AI芯片转移。”他还补充说：“Grace Blackwell系统重近两吨，你不可能很快把它装进口袋或背包里。因此这些系统相当容易追踪……但重要的是，我们销售给的国家和公司都认识到转移是不被允许的，大家都希望继续购买Nvidia技术，因此他们会非常仔细地自我监控，对此相当谨慎。”在这些AI芯片走私传言甚嚣尘上之际，负责执行美国贸易制裁的工业与安全局被认定“能力不足”且资金短缺，一直依赖过时的人工流程来执行对中国科技公司的限制。尽管如此，世界各地仍有公司和个人因绕过华盛顿出口管制而被调查和逮捕。新加坡当局在2025年初捣毁了一个为中国AI实验室DeepSeek走私Nvidia GPU的团伙，突袭22个地点并逮捕9人。同年10月，一家由Alice Huang领导的新加坡公司Megaspeed被指转移了价值20亿美元的Nvidia芯片。次月，四名美国人因向中国运送400块Nvidia A100并试图再发送50块Nvidia H200 GPU而被捕。约四个月后，一起更大的走私丑闻曝光：三名Super Micro员工因向中国走私价值25亿美元的Nvidia硬件被捕，嫌疑人包括公司联合创始人Yih-Shyan“Wally”Liaw，但Super Micro本身未被牵连。该案遍及全球，台湾当局于2026年5月突袭12个相关地点，6月又调查9个地点和6人。黄仁勋在逮捕和突袭后敦促该公司整改出口管制合规，对媒体表示：“我们坚持合作伙伴必须合规。我们希望他们加强和改进监管合规，防止此类事件再次发生。”但就在他发表该声明仅五个月后，一项惊人的指控让一切崩塌。

2026年10月29日，《纽约时报》报道称，黄仁勋可能通过一位与他“关系密切”的公司高管——Alice Huang——成为中国间谍行动的目标。Nvidia否认该指控，公司发言人对Tom's Hardware表示：“Megaspeed与许多其他区域云客户并无不同。黄仁勋与Huang女士的互动并不异常或出人意料。与客户会面是CEO工作的一部分；黄仁勋每年与数千名客户高管交谈。我们的区域云客户收到的是普通商业信息——并非敏感的Nvidia商业秘密——以及零国家安全相关信息。”但仅过了一周多，美国情报来源称这位前Nvidia掌门人与Megaspeed高管有婚外情。Megaspeed正是被指控走私价值20亿美元Nvidia芯片的公司。到11月8日周日晚，黄仁勋承认了这段婚外情，但未在声明中点明第三方身份。许多政府官员通常会对科技高管的私人生活睁一只眼闭一只眼，但他是美国首屈一指的AI芯片制造商领导人，且与总统关系密切，这引起了当局注意。美国国会要求他参加闭门会议，讨论Nvidia“针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议”，FBI也调查了他与该疑似中国间谍的关系。承认与指控引发人们对Alice Huang的深入挖掘。《The Information》的调查显示，她与一个横跨新加坡、中国和英属维尔京群岛的“迷宫”般公司网络有关，据称她帮助转移了约75亿美元的AI GPU进口。其中20亿美元从Megaspeed流向其马来西亚子公司Speedmatrix，另有46亿美元直接从这家新加坡公司流入中国云服务公司上海世纪利通。据报道，她还从其他渠道购买Nvidia GPU，使其进口总值达到估算水平。接近她的人士称，她会利用与黄仁勋的关系招揽客户，经常在微信账号上发布与他的合影，向潜在客户展示与这位Nvidia掌门人的未公开照片，甚至夸口说他会带她共进晚餐并在她生日时送礼物。Alice Huang似乎并非单独行动。多名消息人士称，她的丈夫Kang Wei是获取AI GPU行动的核心人物。他甚至似乎认可她与黄仁勋的关系，并曾开玩笑说她是这位亿万富翁的私人助理。然而，压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草似乎是另一项指控：黄仁勋与另一名女性——公司直接向他汇报的医疗健康副总裁Kimberly Powell——有婚外情。这一消息曝光数小时后，公司董事会宣布黄仁勋辞去Nvidia所有领导职务，员工称他离开这家他花费30多年打造的公司时看起来“破碎而崩溃”。Nvidia正在寻找内部和外部CEO人选，首席财务官Colette Kress担任临时首席执行官。

这可能是一个时代的终结，但未必是黄仁勋的终结。尽管他突然倒台并被迅速逐出Nvidia，他作为AI基础设施之王的地位对AI行业仍有价值。埃隆·马斯克甚至在X上表示，雇用他“将是一种荣幸”，这对任何想进入半导体领域的企业都可能成立。但他是否还想回归？黄仁勋辞职后首次公开声明于11月17日发布在X上，这位前CEO表示“Nvidia员工、投资者、商业伙伴和客户纷纷打电话给我，要求我回归CEO职位”，如果公司董事会要求，他将“荣幸”地接受这份工作。超过19万名股东、合作伙伴、现任和前任员工及粉丝，包括马斯克和Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney，签署了一份在线请愿书，要求让他重新领导公司。美国总统特朗普呼吁恢复他的Nvidia CEO职位。然而董事会可能不这么看。多篇报道称，董事会并未考虑让黄仁勋回归，而是专注于新候选人、对黄仁勋的持续调查以及为国家安全调查做准备。相关事件还包括：Nvidia诞生地Denny's卡座纪念牌在丑闻后被移除（后已恢复），上面标记着“开启万亿美元公司的卡座”；马斯克签署请愿书要求恢复黄仁勋职位，超过13万人签名，但并非所有Nvidia员工都支持他回归；特朗普呼吁恢复黄仁勋Nvidia items.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now
items.description: New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC.
