items.content: New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops like the ASUS ProArt GR1X mini PC are built to run personal AI agents 24/7. RTX Spark desktops are equipped with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. Ten-gigabit Ethernet connectivity enables fast transfers of large datasets, model files and creative assets between RTX Spark compact desktops and networked storage. This advanced hardware unlocks incredible capabilities for creators, developers and AI enthusiasts, including: Running massive 120-billion-parameter large language models locally Rendering 90GB+ 3D scenes in real time Smoothly editing 4:2:2 video in real time The MSI EdgeMesa N AI+ Series RTX Spark compact desktop. New compact desktops are available for purchase from ASUS, Dell and MSI, joining the RTX Spark family of laptops available today. Mini PCs from Acer, GIGABYTE and HP are coming soon, along with the Microsoft Surface RTX Spark Dev Box. From Local Agents to AI Creation Native CUDA support and Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux give developers a foundation for building and running local AI workflows. Developers can set up agents with Hermes Agent or NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and fine-tune supported models using Unsloth. RTX Spark can run creative agents that connect familiar applications and local AI tools, helping creators move from an idea to finished work with natural-language instructions. NVIDIA Switchyard, now available in Hermes, automatically routes agent tasks between local and cloud models. Everyday tasks can run on device, while advanced reasoning draws on cloud models, helping manage cloud costs across creative workflows. These capabilities come together in creative workflows that connect Photoshop and ComfyUI through Hermes Agent. Using natural-language instructions, creators can turn sketches into rendered images and animations, or animate an image entirely on device — from isolating a subject and defining its motion to generating the finished video. NVIDIA brought these workflows to life at Adobe MAX, where attendees used natural-language instructions to turn sketches into rendered images and animations for a shared digital Miami landscape. The RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR features, already available in ComfyUI, extend the pipeline: a generated clip can be expanded to 60 frames per second and converted to high dynamic range for color grading, all within a single ComfyUI workflow on RTX Spark. Adobe Accelerates the Full Creative Stack for RTX Spark NVIDIA and Adobe are expanding native Windows on Arm support and RTX acceleration across Adobe’s creative applications, helping video editors, photographers, designers and 3D artists work more efficiently on RTX Spark. Adobe Premiere accelerates a range of AI-powered editing features through NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX, including Enhance Speech, Object Mask, Scene Edit Detection and Auto Reframe — so editors spend less time waiting and more time cutting. GPU acceleration also extends to Film Impact transition and effects plug-ins. The update improves support for professional video formats, including Canon RAW, Red RAW, ARRI RAW, ARRICORE, ARRI HDE, H.264 and HEVC in MXF, ProRes RAW and long-GOP video. This lets editors realize more than 50% quicker turnaround on everyday H.264 video deliverables. Blender 5.3 Adds DLSS Ray Reconstruction to the Viewport Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction into the Cycles viewport, helping artists evaluate lighting and materials with near-final-quality ray-traced previews as they work. items.titleZh: NVIDIA RTX Spark紧凑型台式机现已上市
items.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA 宣布，华硕、戴尔和微星的新款 RTX Spark 紧凑型台式机即日起上市，定位为专门运行本地 AI 的 Windows PC。该类产品面向开发者、创作者和 AI 爱好者，可在本地运行 AI 智能体、图像与视频生成、模型微调，并让智能体和计划任务 24 小时常驻运行；与笔记本配合时，台式机可承担持续计算，笔记本则用于移动办公或其他任务。

硬件方面，RTX Spark 台式机搭载 20 核 NVIDIA Grace CPU、拥有 6,144 个 CUDA 核心的 NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU，以及最高 128GB 统一内存，AI 性能最高达 1 petaflop，并配备 10GbE 以太网，便于在本地与网络存储之间传输大型数据集、模型文件和创作素材。统一内存和 NVIDIA AI 软件栈使系统能够本地运行最高 1200 亿参数的大语言模型、实时渲染 90GB 以上的 3D 场景，并流畅实时编辑 4:2:2 视频。华硕 ProArt GR1X 迷你主机等产品强调可全天候运行个人 AI 智能体；微星 EdgeMesa N AI+ 系列也在首批产品之列。宏碁、技嘉、惠普的迷你主机以及微软 Surface RTX Spark Dev Box 将后续推出。

软件生态同步扩展。RTX Spark 笔记本和紧凑台式机获得更多创作与开发工作流支持：Adobe 推出原生 Windows on Arm 应用，Blender 集成 DLSS Ray Reconstruction，ComfyUI 支持本地生成流程。开发者可通过原生 CUDA、Windows Subsystem for Linux 中的 Linux 开发工具、Hermes Agent 或 NVIDIA NemoClaw 蓝图构建本地智能体，并使用 Unsloth 微调模型。NVIDIA Switchyard 已集成到 Hermes，可在本地与云端模型之间自动路由任务：日常任务在设备端运行，复杂推理调用云端模型，以控制云成本。创作者还可通过 Hermes Agent 连接 Photoshop 与 ComfyUI，用自然语言把草图转为渲染图像或动画，并在设备端完成主体分离、运动定义和视频生成。ComfyUI 中已有的 RTX Video Frame Generation 和 RTX Video HDR 可将生成片段扩展到 60fps 并转为 HDR，用于调色。

Adobe 方面，NVIDIA 与 Adobe 正扩大原生 Windows on Arm 支持和 RTX 加速。Premiere 通过 NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX 加速 Enhance Speech、Object Mask、Scene Edit Detection、Auto Reframe 等 AI 功能，并改进对 Canon RAW、Red RAW、ARRI RAW、ARRICORE、ARRI HDE、MXF 中的 H.264/HEVC、ProRes RAW 和长 GOP 视频等专业格式的支持，使日常 H.264 视频交付周转时间提升 50% 以上。Photoshop 为 Remove Tool 增加 TensorRT-RTX 加速，并加入 Arm 原生 Camera Raw 支持。Substance 3D Painter 12.2 首次以公开测试形式原生支持 Arm，可在 RTX Spark 上无需兼容层运行。Illustrator 和 InDesign 也推出原生 Windows on Arm 版本，其中 Illustrator 性能较仿真版本最高提升 30%。Blender 5.3 将 DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction 引入 Cycles 视口，让艺术家在交互预览中实时获得接近最终质量的灯光、反射和材质效果，减少噪点预览等待；该功能需要 Blender 5.3 及最新 NVIDIA Game Ready 或 Studio 驱动。

在企业与开发者平台方面，微软 Ignite 宣布 Windows Server 2028 将支持 NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows，该平台基于 GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip，面向在企业应用和数据附近运行 AI 的需求，并扩展加速推理和本地智能体工作负载的硬件选择。Windows ML 更新允许开发者从 Hugging Face 引入任意 GGUF 模型，并通过 llama.cpp 后端在 Windows ML 中运行；实验性的 DxCGC 后端可通过 DirectX 12 编译和运行机器学习模型，使游戏开发者能在图形负载旁执行 AI 工作负载。Windows API 还为 AION Instruct 和 VSR 增加 GPU 支持，开发者可用命令行界面为 Windows ML 构建高性能 AI 模型。

此外，NVIDIA 汇总了本地 AI 生态的最新进展：llama.cpp v1.0.0 发布，带来 API 版本管理、扩展模型支持以及面向 NVFP4 推理的 CUDA 优化；Ricursive Intelligence 推出首个开放模型 Ripple-65B Preview，基于 NVIDIA B300 GPU 训练、使用 Nemotron 后训练数据集，并可在 DGX Spark 本地运行；Runway 发布 270 亿参数的世界动作模型 Praxis-1，可同时预测视频和动作，支持在 GeForce RTX 5090、RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell、DGX Spark 和 DGX Station 上本地运行，并可通过 LoRA 微调适配不同机器人、摄像头和任务；NVIDIA TensorRT Edge-LLM 可通过少量命令在 DGX Spark 上本地运行 AI 模型，并提供下载 Nemotron-3.5 Lightning、优化推理、测试提示词及通过本地 OpenAI 兼容 API 提供服务的教程。整体来看，RTX Spark 通过“统一内存硬件 + 本地 AI 软件栈 + 原生 Arm 应用 + 云端协同路由”，把本地大模型、智能体、创作生成和开发工作流整合到一台 Windows PC 上，强调数据留在本地、降低按 token 计费的云 API 成本，并扩展常驻 AI 与专业创作场景。

items.title: Nvidia board faction angling for Jensen Huang return as CEO, report claims
items.description: Despite Nvidia's board saying it has no intention of bringing former CEO Jensen Huang back to the company, some directors are reportedly still pushing for that to happen.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 26 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Even though Nvidia says that it does not plan to bring its former CEO Jensen Huang back to the company, that hasn't stopped some of its board members from continuing to lobby for his return. Following the news that some of Huang's allies have formed a "war room" to drive his reinstatement just days after his resignation, one Nvidia employee went so far as to warn that the company faces the possibility of an exodus of "irreplaceable talent" if Huang isn't reinstated. We've even seen U.S. President Trump argue for giving Huang his old job back, but the company said during its November 17 earnings call that wasn't in the cards. Now, Semafor reports that some Nvidia board members aren't taking "no" for an answer.Huang, for his part, has already said that he would be "honored" to return to the company that he resigned from in disgrace just a few days ago. At the time, he admitted to having an affair with a woman who worked for Megaspeed, a controversial Nvidia customer linked to the smuggling of export-controlled AI hardware into China. That woman has also been accused of being a Chinese spy, further complicating an already troublesome matter for Nvidia and Huang. Huang and Nvidia's top lawyer will make an appearance before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees in early December and are likely to face some difficult questions.But despite all of this, Huang is said to have spoken with at least one Nvidia board member about the possibility of making a return to Nvidia. That meeting took place hours before Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the company’s earnings call that Huang wasn't coming back. The board voted unanimously to accept his resignation, and won't be backtracking. It's reported that three board members don't agree with that stance, while others have already turned their attention to who will replace Huang long-term. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have also chimed in, while a Taiwanese skyscraper was used to send messages of support to a man who has proven hugely popular in the country. items.titleZh: 英伟达董事会派系图谋让黄仁勋重返CEO职位，报道称
items.descriptionZh:
这则报道聚焦英伟达（Nvidia）前CEO Jensen Huang（黄仁勋）辞职后引发的人事与治理风波。尽管英伟达公开表示不计划让Huang回归，但部分董事会成员仍在继续游说其复职。Huang辞职后数日内，其盟友已成立“作战室”推动其重新上任；一名英伟达员工甚至警告，若Huang不复职，公司可能面临“不可替代人才”流失。美国总统特朗普也公开主张让Huang恢复原职，但英伟达在11月17日财报电话会上明确表示这不在计划之内。Semafor随后报道称，一些董事会成员并不接受这一“不”的答复。

Huang本人已表示，若能回到这家他不久前“蒙羞辞职”的公司，将感到“荣幸”。报道披露，他辞职的直接背景是承认与Megaspeed一名女员工有婚外情。Megaspeed是一家有争议的英伟达客户，被指与将受出口管制的AI硬件走私进入中国有关；该女子还被指控为中国间谍，使事件对英伟达和Huang而言更加复杂。Huang和英伟达首席律师将于12月初出席美国众议院外交事务委员会、情报委员会和中国特别委员会听证会，预计将面对尖锐质询。

尽管争议缠身，报道称Huang至少与一名英伟达董事会成员讨论过回归可能性，而这次会面发生在英伟达董事长Harvey Jones在财报电话会上表示Huang不会回来之前数小时。董事会曾一致投票接受其辞职，且不会逆转这一决定；但据报有三名董事不同意该立场，其他董事则已把注意力转向长期继任者。临时CEO Colette Kress不被考虑作为Huang的全职接替者。Arm CEO Rene Haas被视为头号热门人选，据信董事会已与其接触；Marvell CEO Matt Murphy也在考虑范围内，但外界持续呼吁Huang回归据称让他有所退缩。除部分董事外，SpaceX CEO Elon Musk和Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney也公开声援Huang，台湾一栋摩天大楼还被用来发送支持信息。

需要说明的是，原文并未涉及AI芯片的技术原理、创新点、性能参数或产品对比数据，因此无法从该报道中提炼相关技术细节。其核心影响集中在公司治理、领导层稳定性、出口合规与政府关系层面；对英伟达这类AI芯片企业而言，高管更迭争议和出口管制相关听证可能影响客户信心、人才保留及政策沟通。

items.content: Nvidia has stopped sending its advanced AI chips to China despite the approval it received from the White House to do so in December last year. The announcement was made by interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress during an earnings call on Tuesday, marking a notable shift for the company that, under former CEO Jensen Huang, fought for the right to ship its powerful Hopper architecture H200 chips to China.“Our guidance ⁠does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping ​licenced Hopper data center products to China,” Kress said. She did not explain why Nvidia was ceasing its H200 processor shipments or clarify whether Nvidia would pursue other business with China in the future.The pivot comes after Huang stepped down from his position as Nvidia CEO last week following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, one with a woman who was suspected by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia already faced difficulties around offloading the AI chips prior to this scandal, however. Concerns were raised about failings to properly vet Chinese companies that were approved to handle the H200 AI chips. Reuters also reported earlier this month that around 600,000 ⁠H200 chips ​were stuck in Hong Kong after Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports, with China seeking to reduce its dependency on US technology.

items.titleZh: 英伟达不再向中国出售AI芯片
items.descriptionZh:
Nvidia已停止向中国发送其先进AI芯片，尽管该公司去年12月曾获得白宫批准。临时CEO Colette Kress在周二的财报电话会上宣布，公司业绩指引中不再包含任何获许可的Hopper数据中心产品，并且“不再向中国运送获许可的Hopper数据中心产品”。她没有解释停止H200处理器出货的原因，也未说明Nvidia未来是否会在中国开展其他业务。

这一转向的背景是，Nvidia前CEO黄仁勋曾积极争取向中国出口基于Hopper架构的H200芯片。原文称，黄仁勋上周辞去CEO职务，此前有报道称其涉及多起婚外情，其中一名女性被美国情报部门怀疑为中国间谍。不过，Nvidia在丑闻之前就已面临AI芯片出货难题：一方面，外界担忧公司未能充分审查获准处理H200的中国企业；另一方面，路透本月早些时候报道，约60万颗H200芯片因北京未批准大规模进口而滞留香港，中国正寻求降低对美国技术的依赖。

从技术定位看，H200属于Nvidia Hopper架构的高端数据中心AI加速器，是H100的内存升级版本，采用HBM3e高带宽内存，重点提升大模型训练和推理所需的内存容量与带宽，并延续Transformer Engine等面向生成式AI的能力。原文未披露具体性能参数；公开资料通常将H200描述为在H100基础上显著提升内存容量和带宽，因而更适合大语言模型、生成式AI、云计算数据中心和科学计算等场景。正因如此，H200成为美国出口管制和中国进口审批共同关注的敏感产品。

影响上看，即便美方发放许可，Nvidia对华高端AI芯片供应仍受中方进口审批、合规审查和地缘政治因素制约。约60万颗H200滞留香港的数据，显示潜在渠道库存和中方审批瓶颈的规模。停止出货将限制Nvidia中国数据中心业务收入，也可能推动中国客户更多转向国产AI芯片或现有库存渠道，并加剧全球AI芯片供应链的分化。Kress未给出未来中国业务计划，后续走向将取决于许可范围、中方进口政策以及Nvidia替代产品的合规安排。

items.title: China threatens 'countermeasures' in the face of new AI GPU rental and export restrictions
items.description: China threatens "countermeasures" on the face of new Blackwell rental and export restrictions — Sino-American trade war may be renewed for a new season
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Yesterday, the Trump administration extended the reach of its existing export controls on high-end AI accelerator chips, namely, but not limited to, Nvidia's Blackwell lineup. The updated regulation now requires licenses for renting those chips in large quantities to the entirety of America's D:5 countries list (nations embargoed from arms sales). As expected, the news landed in Beijing like a lead dragon, and its Ministry of Commerce states that China "will take countermeasures to firmly safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests."Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedThe bold move taken by the U.S. arrives at a peculiar time, as President Trump is currently visiting the nation for the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Trump is scheduled to meet President Xi Jinping on Thursday, Nov. 19, a tête-a-tête that's bound to be interesting. Both nations were recently embroiled in a bitter trade war, with ever-mounting tariffs and restrictions on both sides until a temporary truce was called in Oct. 2025. Only some restrictions were lifted, though; for example, Chinese semiconductors still face a 50% tariff when imported stateside.A potential restart of tariff-slapping would all but guarantee an even larger amount of turmoil in U.S. stock markets. Those seas are already choppy enough thanks to Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang's romantic involvement with purported Chinese spy Alice Huang — along with mounting suspicions that the soulmates may have connived to siphon billions' worth of Blackwell chips from her Singaporean outfit Megaspeed onto Chinese AI laboratories.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Nvidia cut off about half of its Asian buyers last July, seemingly in the purview of the export controls, and told data center operators that over 50% of their business must come from non-Chinese companies. Meanwhile, both Malaysia and Singapore have intensified their scrutiny of AI hardware shipments.China's countermeasures ammo is as of yet unspecified. The nation had restricted the sale of gallium, germanium, and antimony to the U.S. previously, and the truce shelved that bullet until Nov. 2027. Beijing may well choose to simply not renew that agreement when that day comes. Although analysts believe that the nations will be cordial enough during this summit, Trump's perceived provocation may bring China's proverbial nuclear option of restricting rare earth exports back to the loading bay. You may like Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China New US rules aim to restrict Chinese firms’ remote access to AI servers and infrastructure Nvidia cracks down on overseas cloud AI GPU rentals for China The truce on that particular matter only has a few weeks left, expiring on Jan. 10, 2027. Likewise, super-hard materials and high-density lithium batteries, crucial for the newest generations of EVs, solar power storage, and battery installations, all have white flags that will come down early next year. Analysts also expect that Chinese firms and their government will continue to heavily invest in domestic chip production, namely, but not only, by Huawei.Broadly speaking, the U.S.' updated chip control regulation means that Chinese firms cannot sidestep the existing control on chip sales by renting them instead, closing one of the main existing loopholes around the export restrictions. items.titleZh: 面对新的AI GPU租赁和出口限制，中国威胁采取“反制措施”
items.descriptionZh:
美国特朗普政府昨日进一步扩大高端AI加速器芯片出口管制的适用范围，覆盖英伟达Blackwell系列等产品，并将“大量租用”这类芯片纳入许可证要求，适用对象扩大至美国“D:5国家”武器禁运名单上的全部国家。所谓D:5名单包括中国、俄罗斯等被美国列入武器禁运的国家。新规的核心变化在于：过去管制主要针对芯片销售，中国企业理论上可通过境外云服务商租用算力绕过限制；现在，大规模租赁高端AI芯片同样需要许可证，等于堵住了“以租代购”的主要漏洞。同时，向印度尼西亚、马来西亚、新加坡、泰国、巴西等国销售相关芯片也需申请许可证，因为美国商务部怀疑这些国家存在进口Blackwell转售中国的渠道。

这一政策出台的背景是中美芯片与贸易博弈持续升级。两国此前经历了一轮加征关税和出口限制的贸易战，直到2025年10月才达成临时休战，但只是部分限制被解除，中国半导体产品进入美国仍面临50%关税。原文称，特朗普正赴深圳出席APEC峰会，并计划于11月19日与中国领导人会晤；在这一敏感节点扩大芯片管制，被视为对华施压。中国商务部已回应称，将采取反制措施，坚定维护国家主权、安全和发展利益，但具体反制工具尚未公布。

从技术层面看，Blackwell是英伟达面向数据中心的新一代AI加速器平台，主要用于大模型训练和推理，依赖高算力GPU、高带宽内存和高速互连，是当前先进AI基础设施的核心部件。报道没有给出Blackwell具体算力、显存带宽等性能参数，因此无法进行芯片级性能对比；其重点在监管逻辑创新：美国不再只卡“芯片实物出口”，而是把“算力租赁”和“第三国转口”纳入管制链条，试图从云服务、分销渠道和区域转口三个环节限制中国获取先进AI算力。应用场景上，这类芯片主要服务AI数据中心、云计算平台、大模型训练与推理集群；管制收紧将直接影响中国AI实验室和云厂商获取先进算力，也会波及亚洲的数据中心运营商、云租赁商和硬件分销商。

原文还提到，英伟达曾在7月切断约一半亚洲买家的业务，并要求数据中心运营商保证超过50%的业务来自非中国公司；马来西亚和新加坡也在加强对AI硬件货运的审查。市场层面，若关税和出口限制重新升级，可能进一步加剧美国股市波动。原文还夹杂了关于英伟达亚洲分销渠道、新加坡Megaspeed涉嫌将Blackwell转售至中国AI实验室的疑虑，以及针对黄仁勋个人关系的未经证实指控，摘要对此不展开。中国可能的反制选项包括此前对镓、锗、锑实施的对美出口限制，该措施在休战框架下暂缓至2027年11月，北京可能到期不再续约；稀土出口管制被视为更强硬手段，超硬材料和高密度锂电池等关键物项的限制豁免也将在明年初到期。分析人士预计，无论外部管制如何变化，中国企业和政府仍会继续加大对本土芯片产业的投资，华为是重点之一。总体而言，新规将高端AI芯片的管制从“卖芯片”延伸到“租算力”和“第三国转口”，短期内加大中国获取先进AI算力的难度，也可能推动中国本土AI芯片和算力基础设施加速替代。

history.content: New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president of education, told the Times that, “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and that schools that turn off Google’s AI features “will not have access to Search.”Many elected officials, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, responded harshly, calling Google’s behavior “extortion.” Mamdani had recently announced a policy that barred 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom. In a statement to the Times, New York City schools chancellor Kamar H. Samuels said, “If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options.” Chicago’s public schools have also reportedly told Google that if it can’t provide a version of Search without AI, “the district will look to other search solutions.”In a statement to The Verge, Google spokesperson Laura Breen said, “We hear parents and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to shortcut learning, and we share the same goal: help students learn. To improve Search for the classroom, we’re starting to pilot Guided Learning capabilities in Search this month to walk students step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers. Next year, we’re also updating our approach to controls for schools to address feedback we’ve heard from educators, so Gemini app, Gemini Notebook and Search will be off by default until schools decide which services to enable. We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers.”Educators are wary of AI’s effect on students’ critical thinking skills, and some studies have shown that students who use AI generally perform worse on tests. There are also concerns about the mental health effects on children who develop relationships with chatbots at a young age. But Google is deeply embedded in classrooms across the US, which rely on Google Classroom, Chromebooks, and other services, and going fully Google-free might prove difficult.

history.titleZh: 全美最大的几个学区考虑弃用谷歌搜索
history.descriptionZh:
据《纽约时报》报道，纽约、洛杉矶和芝加哥的学校正在考虑改用Google搜索的替代方案。原因是Google表示，如果学校选择退出其AI功能，公司将禁用这些学校的Search服务。从明年开始，学校将无法在保留Search的同时单独关闭由Gemini驱动的功能；换句话说，学校若想禁用Gemini相关AI功能，就必须同时放弃Search。Google教育业务副总裁Chris Phillips对《纽约时报》称，“Search和AI已经深度整合”，关闭Google的AI功能意味着学校“将无法访问Search”。

这一做法引发多名民选官员强烈批评。纽约市市长Zohran Mamdani和参议员Bernie Sanders称Google的行为是“勒索”。Mamdani最近宣布政策，禁止2-K-8学生在课堂使用AI。纽约市学校总监Kamar H. Samuels表示，如果Google不重新考虑立场，纽约市将探索其他搜索选项。芝加哥公立学校也 reportedly 告知Google，如果不能提供不含AI的Search版本，该学区将寻找其他搜索解决方案。

从技术角度看，这一争议的核心是Google将生成式AI能力嵌入搜索产品架构：搜索不再只是返回链接，而是结合Gemini提供摘要、对话和引导式解答。Google发言人对The Verge表示，公司理解家长和教师担心学生用AI“走捷径”学习，但双方目标一致，都是帮助学生学习的。Google本月开始在Search中试点“Guided Learning”能力，不再只给出快速答案，而是分步骤引导学生解决复杂问题。Google还称，明年将更新面向学校的控制方案，以回应教育者反馈：Gemini应用、Gemini Notebook和Search将默认关闭，直到学校决定启用哪些服务。Google表示正在与教育者合作构建这些体验。

背景上，美国教育界对生成式AI进入课堂持谨慎态度，担忧其削弱学生批判性思维。一些研究显示，使用AI的学生在测试中通常表现更差；也有人担心儿童过早与聊天机器人建立关系会影响心理健康。但Google在美国课堂中嵌入很深，学校广泛依赖Google Classroom、Chromebooks等服务，完全“去Google化”可能并不容易。此次事件反映出学校对教学自主权、学生隐私和AI使用边界的关切，与Google将AI深度整合进搜索和教育生态的商业与技术路线之间的冲突。若纽约、洛杉矶、芝加哥等大型学区转向替代搜索方案，可能影响Google在教育市场的产品采用和学校采购决策。报道未披露具体性能指标或成本对比数据。

history.title: AMD’s Twitter brag that it ‘loves gamers’ met with savage Community Note
history.description: Following a post on X, AMD Japan's claim that the company values gamers "above all else" saw those gamers point out that its own CEO believes the company is more focused on data centers.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter AMD Japan's X account has been met with sharp reproach after claiming the company loves gamers and values its interactions with gamers above all else, with commenters and even a community note expressing dissent at the sentiment, owing to AMD's comments on its "data center-first" ethos and a commitment to AI that has driven the price of consumer PC gaming up to nearly unaffordable levels.Quoting a Tom's Hardware post on the X social network discussing CEO Dr. Lisa Su meeting gamers and autographing a GPU, the AMD Japan account was quick to seize the moment. "AMD values its interactions with gamers above all else," the post read, but it was met with a stark reminder that gamers don't feel the same way. The post soon received a new community note that pointed out that AMD's own CEO doesn't agree. In fact, Su was quoted as saying that AMD is now "a data center-first company," with the note also pointing to the fact that AMD's data center revenue increased 97% year-over-year, as per its Q3 2026 earnings report. That equates to around $8.5 billion in revenue, while client and gaming revenue fell 8% to $3.7 billion. Gaming alone was down 40%.At the time, Su said that AMD expected its server revenue to double year over year in 2027, with its data center AI revenue growing at an even faster rate. "As a result, we expect data center to be more than eighty percent of our total revenue in 2027 and to drive the majority of our revenue and earnings growth," the CEO said during the company's earnings call.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: ゲーマーとの交流を何よりも大切にするAMD。 コミュニティと直接つながり、その声に耳を傾け続ける姿勢こそAMDの強みです。 AMD loves gamers. 🎮November 17, 2026By comparison, the same call heard Su say that, in 2027, AMD was "planning for PC market unit shipments to decline by a double-digit percentage." With this all in mind, it's perhaps no surprise that the AMD Japan X account stirred such a strong response from gamers who feel that AMD has left them behind in search of a more lucrative data center market. AMD is certainly not alone in that regard. Nvidia, once the darling of the PC component enthusiast, is now focused on AI data center components instead. The company's high-performance AI chips are so capable that they're export-controlled, something that, among other reasons, will put former CEO Jensen Huang in front of a House Foreign Affairs panel in December.As for AMD, its ill-timed, misjudged X post ended with "AMD loves gamers." Gamers would appear to disagree. history.content: If someone handed you $8,300 every second, what would you do? That’s how much pure profit Nvidia now makes. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, Nvidia will likely have cleared $45,000 and change. It’s easy to look at Nvidia, a company that just lost its visionary founder CEO due to a series of scandals, and think that the company and maybe the entire AI industry are in terrible trouble. Perhaps so?RelatedAn overview of Jensen Huang’s messy daysJensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEOBut I want you to understand: Nvidia isn’t your average semi-successful company that might tempt a new CEO to fix things that are broken. It is a company so staggeringly, mind-bogglingly successful it’ll do everything in its power not to rock the boat. There is so much money at stake.It’s so much money that when I heard about Jensen Huang’s resignation, my first thought was: I need a way to visualize this jaw-dropping amount of money for you. I want to show you that Nvidia has risen so far, so fast, that rival chipmakers AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm barely qualify as competition now. If you’re on a desktop OS, you could mouse over each dot in our chart above to see the staggering sums. But we built another way to visualize the rise of Nvidia I like even better. It’s a horizontal bar graph that not only puts Nvidia’s revenue growth in perspective, but shows you its monster profits right alongside them — plus the world events that made Nvidia a star. TL;DR: The crypto boom and the great GPU shortage have nothing on the AI boom. Those earlier periods saw Nvidia’s profits briefly peak at $1.24 billion and $3 billion a quarter respectively, while the rise of data centers has driven them to $65 billion per quarter with no sign of stopping.Yes, Jensen may have set a trillion dollars of Nvidia’s market cap on fire — from around $5 trillion at the start of November to “only” $3.6 trillion now — but the smoldering company is raking in $700 million in profit a day on average.Put another way: Nvidia could give a $1 million bonus to every one of its 42,000 employees, every three months, without running out of cash. Or, you know, Nvidia could end world hunger or provide clean water for everyone, now that it’s making over $200 billion in pure profit a year.Maybe that’d make people feel differently about data centers? But even if we stick to self-serving capitalism, you’re probably still a happy investor if you bought Nvidia a decade ago. A $1,000 investment 10 years ago is now worth over $67,000. You’d have over $1 million if you invested $15,000 back then. And make no mistake, Nvidia is sticking to capitalism. Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress just promised to return as much money to investors as possible on the company’s November 17th earnings call. “Going forward, we intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders,” she announced. “All” is a lot more than the 50 percent baseline that Jensen promised five months ago.Nvidia isn’t the only company whose fortunes have risen this dramatically. RAMageddon revealed that just three companies — Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron — controlled nearly 90 percent of the entire global DRAM market, and those three have repeatedly signaled that they’d prefer to celebrate record profits instead of ramping up production too fast. But while their revenues and profits have been skyrocketing even faster over the past year or so, even Big RAM hasn’t caught the AI wave quite the same way as Nvidia. Samsung, of course, doesn’t just make memory — its revenue numbers include phones, tablets, TVs, home appliances, chips, displays, camera sensors, audio, networking equipment, medical equipment, and more.In the most recent quarter, Micron made $37.7 billion in profit, SK Hynix made $29.8 billion, and Samsung came in at around $55.3 billion, but they’re all shy of Nvidia’s $65.3 billion. Historically, RAM has also been a bit more cyclical: Both Micron and SK Hynix actually lost money in 2023 because they produced too much memory.On its latest earnings call, the first since cofounder Jensen Huang’s resignation, interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress reinforced the idea that Nvidia expects the good times to keep on rolling.Asked how things might change under new management, she suggested that they wouldn’t: “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual,” she said. She added that the company has secured the backing of customers and suppliers including TSMC, the all-important firm that actually fabricates Nvidia’s chips.“Our momentum is real, our demand is accelerating, our supply is growing. Our customers and partners are with us, and employees are committed,” she claimed. “We’ve got this.”Nvidia claims it’ll rake in even more money next quarter, with projected revenue of $130 billion. Profit may be proportionally smaller since gross margins are estimated to drop to 71–72 percent (compared to nearly 75 percent), but Kress said Nvidia intends to get them up as high as 73 percent next year.In other words: This astounding gravy train isn’t going anywhere. At least that’s the plan.Stevie Bonifield contributed to this story.

history.titleZh: 英伟达的崛起，可视化呈现
history.descriptionZh:
原文以“每秒净赚8300美元”开篇，称读完一段的时间Nvidia就能入账约4.5万美元，借此强调其盈利规模已到惊人程度。背景是：原文称Nvidia创始人兼CEO黄仁勋因一系列丑闻离职，外界容易因此担心公司和整个AI行业陷入麻烦；但文章强调，Nvidia并非一家需要新CEO“修修补补”的普通公司，而是一家成功到不愿轻易改变方向的巨头，背后牵涉的资金规模太大。文章用收入与利润可视化说明：加密热潮和GPU短缺时期，Nvidia季度利润峰值分别约为12.4亿美元和30亿美元；而AI数据中心需求将其推高至每季度650亿美元，且未见停止迹象。尽管市值从11月初约5万亿美元降至“仅”3.6万亿美元，公司日均利润仍约7亿美元，年纯利润超过2000亿美元。形象地说，Nvidia可以每季度给4.2万名员工每人发100万美元奖金而不至于现金枯竭；十年前投资1000美元，如今价值超过6.7万美元，投资1.5万美元则超过100万美元。

技术逻辑上，原文并未展开具体芯片架构，但核心驱动很清楚：AI数据中心对GPU算力的结构性需求。GPU的大规模并行计算适合大模型训练和推理，数据中心集群把算力变成基础设施，使Nvidia从游戏显卡和加密挖矿周期转向AI基础设施的核心供应商。其供应链和客户关系也被视为关键支撑：临时CEO兼CFO Colette Kress称公司已获得包括台积电在内的客户和供应商支持，并表示“从业务角度看，一切照常”，“势头是真实的，需求在加速，供应在增长”。她还在11月17日财报电话会上承诺，将扣除战略用途后的全部超额自由现金流返还股东，这高于五个月前黄仁勋承诺的50%基线。Nvidia预计下一季度营收达1300亿美元；毛利率预计从近75%降至71%—72%，但计划明年提升至73%。

对比数据方面，文章指出三星、SK海力士和美光三家控制近90%的全球DRAM市场，却更倾向于庆祝创纪录利润而非过快扩产。最近季度利润为：美光377亿美元、SK海力士298亿美元、三星约553亿美元，均低于Nvidia的653亿美元；同时RAM行业周期性更强，美光和SK海力士曾在2023年因供过于求而亏损。总体看，Nvidia的业绩反映了AI数据中心资本开支的强劲势头，应用场景覆盖大模型训练、推理和云端AI基础设施；但高利润、供应链集中和内存周期也提示AI繁荣背后的资本密集与周期性风险。原文结论是：这列“利润列车”短期不会停下，至少这是公司的计划。

history.title: Nvidia promises employee pay raises, equity before December to quell unrest in wake of Jensen Huang scandal
history.description: Interim CEO Collete Kress reportedly offered staffers higher wages and more equity on an advanced schedule at the company's first all-hands after Jensen Huang resigned.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia today held its first all-hands meeting since the resignation of co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. According to Wired, interim CEO Colette Kress offered more money and equity on a faster-than-expected schedule to calm staffers' nerves."So I’m here to tell you, the best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp,” Wired reports Kress said.The pay and equity bumps are set for December, far ahead of the company's normal raise cycle. Kress said that compensation and more clarity from the board were the most common topics in questions submitted ahead of the meeting. Keeping current employees happy will be one of Kress' most important short-term challenges. One director-level employee has already written to the board and top executives, warning that failure to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive could lead to the loss of ‘irreplaceable talent.’A potential exodus of talent could also spook investors, despite standout earnings on Thursday. A leadership crisis could make the company seem less stable, and Huang had placed himself as the anchor point for many decisions and the company's overall vision.Huang has expressed interest in returning to Nvidia, saying he would be "honored" to lead the company again if asked by the board. The board was clear in yesterday's earnings call that it did not intend to bring Huang back, though there is reportedly a pro-Huang faction.Nvidia cofounder Chris Malachowsky was also on the call, explaining that the company lives its values rather than simply plastering them on posters.“We’re going to be fine,” he said. history.descriptionZh:
英伟达在联合创始人、前CEO黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）辞职后召开首次全员大会。据Wired报道，临时CEO科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）在会上宣布，将以快于预期的节奏向员工提供更多现金和股权奖励，以安抚员工情绪。克雷斯表示，公司最重要的是照顾好每一位现有员工，让大家对公司感觉良好、不必担心薪酬。加薪和股权奖励预计在12月落地，明显早于公司正常加薪周期。她还透露，会前员工提交的问题最集中在薪酬和董事会提供更明确信息两方面。

留住现有员工是克雷斯短期内的关键挑战之一。报道称，已有一名总监级员工致信董事会和高管，警告若不能恢复黄仁勋的CEO职位，公司可能失去“不可替代的人才”。潜在的人才外流也可能令投资者不安，尽管英伟达周四公布了亮眼财报。领导层危机可能让公司显得不够稳定，而黄仁勋此前将自己置于许多决策和公司整体愿景的“锚点”位置。黄仁勋已表达回归兴趣，称若董事会邀请，他将“荣幸”再次领导公司。但董事会在前一日财报电话会上明确表示不打算让黄仁勋回归，不过据报道公司内部存在支持黄仁勋的派系。联合创始人克里斯·马拉霍夫斯基（Chris Malachowsky）也在电话会上表示，公司是践行价值观，而不是把价值观贴在海报上，并称“我们会没事的”。

该报道聚焦英伟达领导层交接、薪酬安抚和人才保留，未涉及具体芯片产品或技术参数。对AI芯片公司而言，核心资产高度依赖关键人才和路线图连续性，此次事件的关键影响在于员工士气、人才流失风险以及投资者对公司稳定性的判断。

history.content: If the glorious AI revolution rests entirely on the well-being of one man, AI is perhaps not as robust a technology as I had previously been led to believe. Nonetheless, chunks of Silicon Valley are now insisting he is indispensable. For instance, if Elon Musk is telling the truth, then Jensen Huang (the former CEO of Nvidia, a company with a market cap of about $3 trillion) has been making deals that were “a handshake with Jensen” with suppliers — “not a written contract,” Musk wrote.Fascinating stuff to tell shareholders. But after listening to Nvidia’s first earnings call with its new CEO, Colette Kress, I do think something may have shifted. In her former role as CFO, Kress generally told Huang to stop spending so much money on financing its customers, because telling the CEO to stop spending so much goddamn money is the CFO’s job. Apparently he belittled her about this, but that’s the CEO–CFO relationship, baby! Anyway she’s the boss now, at least temporarily. I think it’s reasonable to assume that though Nvidia has for years been the AI industry’s sugar daddy, without Huang and his handshakes in the picture, it may be less liberal with its cash.Kress shot down the idea that Huang’s departure would lead to a brain drain within NvidiaKress’ job was never going to be easy. Even without tantrums from the likes of Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Musk, both of whom seem to have a lot of free time for guys who are ostensibly running multibillion-dollar companies, having to steer a company after an event on the scale of Huang’s meltdown is a miserable task. But this woman also is now having to deal with a bunch of guys publicly insisting that Huang was the only reason Nvidia succeeded. It amused me on the call that she did the thing I often do when men decide they can bully me, which is to tap in another man who is theoretically or actually in charge of me — and so on the call, Nvidia board Chair Harvey C. Jones politely told these losers to get bent. The board does not intend to reinstate Huang, and the company won’t be taking questions about him.On the call, Kress pointedly noted that Nvidia’s agreements with suppliers last through the end of the decade, so I suppose we must entertain the possibility that when it comes to the handshake deals, Musk is, once again, lying. This is an important thing, though — as SemiAnalysis noted in its bizarrely conspiratorial post on the situation, Nvidia is successful because it has choked off the supply chain.Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46Kress also shot down the idea that Huang’s departure would lead to a brain drain within Nvidia, or the kind of open internal revolt that got Sam Altman reinstated at OpenAI during “the blip” in 2023. She told investors that “our employees, we believe, are committed. They are committed to doing their life’s work at Nvidia.” Nvidia’s employees have “been working seamlessly on what they need to complete,” she added. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual.” I’m sure we’ll hear more about this in the coming days, but unlike with Altman, Huang resigned, and we all know why. And while some employees support reinstating Huang, I notice that there’s a real dearth of “we’ll quit with him” in those sentiments.I don’t think this is going to shut the Branch Nvidians up, but I do think the board doesn’t have another choice here. Hilariously, we learned this weekend that Nvidia did not buy complete directors’ and officers’ insurance. While the individual executives’ and board members’ personal assets are shielded from lawsuits that stem from its executives’ behavior, the company is not. So if someone, or perhaps several someones, were to file a suit because of, say, Huang’s personal life and its damaging effects on the stock price, Nvidia itself is on the hook.The scandal isn’t mainly about the affairs, as much fun as we all have been having with themThis is to say nothing of the Securities and Exchange Commission’s investigation — which, given how cliqued up Huang was with President Donald Trump, may be investigating on his behalf rather than investigating him — or the California attorney general going on Bloomberg TV to say that he was going to start kicking the tires on an investigation, or Huang and general counsel Tim Teter’s upcoming congressional testimony. The three actual lawyers left at the Department of Justice may be doing their own investigation, too. Elizabeth Warren seems mad. Marco Rubio’s name has been publicly attached in stories on the leaks, which makes me a little suspicious about who’s been doing the leaking.A reminder: The scandal isn’t mainly about the affairs, as much fun as we all have been having with them. It is about Nvidia customers allegedly circumventing a ban on selling chips to China. The scandal is already big enough that US policy has been altered; the Department of Commerce informed us all on November 16th that there were new restrictions on selling chips to countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. Also, data centers around the world need licenses from the US to lease compute to companies headquartered in China.“No one could tell them ‘no’ or put them in their place.”You may be wondering how these restrictions will affect Nvidia’s sales. The company also addressed this, though somewhat obliquely: It raised its forecast, saying that revenue will grow by 75 percent next year. Still, given that Singapore alone was responsible for $104 billion of revenue in 2025, I am curious about the number; at the time, it was the second-biggest geographic area by revenue, dwarfed only by the US. I can’t tell you how much Singaporean sales matter to Nvidia now, because around the time that Singaporean sales reportedly started to represent half the company’s revenue, Nvidia switched its reporting methodology. The company had previously noted that “most shipments associated with Singapore revenue were to locations other than Singapore and shipments to Singapore were insignificant.” Notably, Megaspeed had a Singapore address — and was the subject of a truncated Commerce Department investigation into whether its chips were being diverted to China. Fun stuff!You know what else is fun? Jensen Huang’s children are still at the company, at least as far as anyone knows. His daughter Madison, described as Huang’s “chief of staff” by The New York Times, even helped direct Nvidia’s response to inquiries about Megaspeed, which have been mounting now for a year, the Financial Times reported. Her husband, Nico Caprez, “was promoted to a role that covered international deals with cloud computing clients in Asia” around the time those inquiries were getting started. “They had a lot of power and influence and were allowed to operate unchecked,” an anonymous source told the FT. “No one could tell them ‘no’ or put them in their place.”His kids — one of them, Spencer, ran a bar before his role at Nvidia — likely haven’t endeared themselves to their colleagues, based on some of the reporting now trickling out about them. What was Spencer doing at Nvidia? Unknown. “Some executives said they had never encountered Spencer Huang in the course of business,” The Wall Street Journal wrote.As a person who loves mess, I think the Branch Nvidians should keep this shit comingEmploying the CEO’s relatives was already a governance risk. If the outside agitation continues to reinstate Jensen Huang, there are three key lambs that Nvidia can slaughter, and all of them are his relatives. I suppose the thing I find most astonishing is that Huang doesn’t see the writing on the wall; he has posted that if “the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” The post was met with, among other things, Altman posting a green heart in response.Now, as a person who loves mess, I think the Branch Nvidians should keep this shit coming. I mean, Huang can nominate two people to the board of directors before the company’s shareholder meeting next year. Let’s have a stupid proxy fight and see what else leaks about Huang’s leadership and children! Of course, that will be difficult for Kress to manage — but that’s I guess what she’s getting paid for.Up until now, Kress had been trying to rein in Huang’s spending on the AI ecosystem — financing, investments, and so on — in a huge swath of companies, according to stories in The Information and The Wall Street Journal. According to the Journal’s story, Huang noted that the vaunted deals he’d made with suppliers “were coming at him like an ‘avalanche,’” while “major cloud providers were running away from Nvidia.” This does explain Nvidia’s role as the sugar daddy for the neocloud industry. Kress reportedly pushed back on some of its agreements, apparently significantly downsizing a financial commitment to OpenAI among other things. Now, while she’ll be spending plenty of her time managing the fallout from Huang’s departure, she won’t be directly fighting with him over Nvidia’s finances.It publicly tells us there are limitations on what Nvidia is willing to supportOn the earnings call, analyst Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein Research asked about a new paragraph he’d noticed in the earnings release about neoclouds. Nvidia had been supplying guarantees to some neoclouds by saying it would purchase compute if no one else would. The new paragraph reads, in part, “Our commitments take effect only if the neoclouds secure financing to purchase the data center infrastructure products and the related compute capacity is deployed, made operational, and accepted by us.” Kress clarified that this meant that if neoclouds’ buildout was delayed — or they otherwise had a challenge in building the warehouse to stick the chips in — Nvidia’s guarantee “doesn’t exist anymore,” she said. “Is it new? No. Did we change anything? No,” she said.I have no way of knowing if this language had been ready to go in the press release before Huang resigned, but it does seem notable all the same. It publicly tells us there are limitations on what Nvidia is willing to support. And knowing Kress wanted Huang to spend less on this stuff, I think it tees us up for an interesting period. Passing under the radar last week were some indications that the Federal Reserve may be about to do an interest rate hike, which is trouble for a number of companies, such as CoreWeave, that rely on debt for their data center buildouts. If we are entering a period where financing is more expensive or more difficult to get, we may see some neoclouds falter. The new paragraph in the earnings release suggests that Nvidia wants us all to know that it’s not going to bail them out forever. Bring Huang back if you want, I guess, but even he can’t control the Fed — or the increasingly odd outlook for data center financing. In the coming months, Nvidia may be better off with a woman who wants to keep the costs down.You know who is getting money under Kress, though? Nvidia staff. They can expect raises and equity in December.

history.descriptionZh:
这篇带有强烈讽刺和评论色彩的报道，以“黄仁勋卸任、英伟达CFO Colette Kress接任CEO”为背景，讨论英伟达在AI芯片产业链中的权力、治理风险、对华出口管制风波以及新管理层的财务纪律。文章开头提出：如果AI革命完全依赖某一个人，这项技术本身就并不稳健；但硅谷部分人士仍坚称黄仁勋不可替代。马斯克称，黄仁勋与供应商达成的是“与Jensen握手”式协议，而非书面合同。报道认为，若没有黄仁勋及其“握手交易”，英伟达可能不再像过去那样慷慨地为客户和生态伙伴提供资金支持。

在英伟达首次由Kress主持的财报电话会上，Kress否认黄仁勋离职会导致人才流失或内部叛乱，称员工“致力于在英伟达完成毕生工作”，业务“一切如常”。董事会主席Harvey C. Jones则表示董事会不打算恢复黄仁勋职位，也不会回答相关问题。文章还提到，Kress在担任CFO期间曾劝阻黄仁勋过度花钱资助客户；她如今成为CEO，可能意味着英伟达将收紧对AI生态的融资、投资和客户支持。Nvidia与供应商的协议据称持续到本十年末，这使马斯克所谓“握手协议”的说法受到质疑。文章还引用SemiAnalysis观点称，英伟达的成功部分来自对供应链的“卡位”和控制。

报道的核心丑闻并非黄仁勋个人绯闻，而是英伟达客户涉嫌规避对华芯片销售禁令。文章称，美国商务部11月16日宣布对印尼、马来西亚、新加坡、泰国、巴西等国销售芯片实施新限制，并要求全球数据中心在向中国总部企业出租算力时获得美国许可证。相关调查可能涉及SEC、加州总检察长、司法部以及黄仁勋和总法律顾问Tim Teter即将进行的国会作证；文章还提到Elizabeth Warren、Marco Rubio以及泄露事件。英伟达方面则提高业绩预测，称明年收入将增长75%。但文章质疑新加坡销售数据：2025年新加坡曾贡献1040亿美元收入，是仅次于美国的第二大地区；随后英伟达更改报告方法。此前公司称，与新加坡收入相关的大部分出货并非发往新加坡，发往新加坡的出货“不重要”。文章还提到，地址在新加坡的Megaspeed曾受到商务部调查，涉及芯片是否被转运至中国。

治理层面，文章称黄仁勋的子女仍在英伟达任职：女儿Madison被《纽约时报》描述为黄仁勋的“幕僚长”，曾协助指导公司回应Megaspeed相关询问；其丈夫Nico Caprez在相关询问开始前后被提升到负责亚洲云计算客户国际交易的岗位。匿名信源称他们“权力和影响力很大，且不受约束”。儿子Spencer曾在酒吧工作，后在英伟达任职，但《华尔街日报》称一些高管表示在业务中从未遇到过他。文章认为，聘用CEO亲属本身已是治理风险；若外界继续施压要求黄仁勋回归，英伟达可“牺牲”的正是这些亲属。黄仁勋曾发帖称，如果董事会认为他的回归符合股东、员工、公司和美国利益，他愿意回应呼吁回归；Altman以绿色爱心回应。黄还可在明年股东大会前提名两名董事，文章预计可能出现代理权争夺和更多泄露。

财务与业务模式方面，Kress此前试图约束黄仁勋在AI生态中的巨额融资和投资。报道援引《信息》和《华尔街日报》称，黄仁勋曾表示与供应商的交易像“雪崩”般涌来，而主要云厂商却在远离英伟达；这解释了英伟达为何成为“neocloud”（新型云服务商）行业的“金主”。Kress曾反对部分协议，并显著缩减对OpenAI的财务承诺。财报电话会上，分析师Stacy Rasgon注意到财报新增一段关于neocloud担保的表述：英伟达此前承诺，如果无人购买算力，它将购买；新表述则称，只有neocloud获得融资购买数据中心基础设施产品、相关算力部署并运行且被英伟达接受后，承诺才生效。Kress称，如果neocloud建设延迟或遇到建仓库放芯片的困难，担保“就不存在了”，并强调这不是新变化。文章认为，这公开表明英伟达的支持有限度；若美联储加息、债务融资变贵，CoreWeave等依赖债务建设数据中心的neocloud可能受挫，英伟达不会永远兜底。文章最后称，在Kress领导下，英伟达员工预计12月获得加薪和股权。整体看，报道的核心论点是：英伟达的AI芯片优势不仅来自GPU和供应链控制，也来自对客户融资和算力购买承诺的深度介入；黄仁勋离职后，公司正转向更谨慎的成本和风险控制，但治理、出口管制和地缘政治风险仍在发酵。

history.title: Remember the frontier AI pause? Chip companies don’t either
history.description:
Nvidia began shipping its most advanced AI computing system, the Vera Rubin NVL72, calling it the “fastest product ramp in the company’s history.” | Image: Nvidia	

This summer, OpenAI paused its largest planned frontier training run after its AI agents accidentally hacked Hugging Face and early evidence suggested that its next model could independently find and exploit security flaws. Read the full story at The Verge.
history.content: This summer, OpenAI paused its largest planned frontier training run after its AI agents accidentally hacked Hugging Face and early evidence suggested that its next model could independently find and exploit security flaws. In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing advances in the most powerful AI models, warning that they could be used to launch cyberattacks or become harder for their own creators to control.It was a strange moment for the AI boom. The people building the most powerful models were warning about what those models might be capable of, and investors were suddenly wondering what would happen to chip demand if the labs eased up on new models. US chip stocks bore the brunt of the sell-off.“Pumping the brakes on frontier training won’t shrink the AI chip market but it will simply reallocate the spend.”Despite the hubbub it created, whatever slowdown there was appears to have been short-lived. OpenAI had announced only a two-week pause; it restarted the run 10 days later, at the end of August, though it continued to “temporarily hold back some smaller experimental training runs.” Anthropic released upgraded versions of its Fable and Mythos frontier models in November, touting improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision.And the companies selling the chips powering those advances are doing better than ever.Nvidia on Tuesday posted a blockbuster quarter, with data center revenue rising 110 percent from a year ago to $107.6 billion in the three months ended October 25. The chip designer began shipping its most advanced AI computing system, the Vera Rubin NVL72, calling it the “fastest product ramp in the company’s history.” The Rubin platform generated nearly $20 billion in revenue in its first quarter of production shipments alone. The racks are already running at CoreWeave, Google, Microsoft, and Oracle. Meta plans to expand Vera Rubin deployments to train and run AI models and agents.Nvidia name-dropped Anthropic and OpenAI, too. Anthropic has expanded access to Vera Rubin capacity through cloud providers and continues to work with Nvidia on future chip designs tailored to its workloads. OpenAI is among the companies adopting Nvidia’s new Vera CPUs.“Proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic continue to advance the frontier,” Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress said on the earnings call. She said the company expects major frontier labs to account for approximately 15 percent of its data center revenue this fiscal year. Nvidia also raised its revenue growth forecast for next fiscal year from 70 percent to 75 percent.RelatedQualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sinkAMD rides data center riches to ‘largest and most profitable’ quarter in historyIntel says it’s selling every affordable laptop chip it can makeChipmaker AMD, meanwhile, reported its biggest quarter ever earlier this month, with revenue up 45 percent to $13.4 billion. Data center sales drove that growth, nearly doubling to $8.5 billion. OpenAI and Anthropic were among the first customers running workloads on AMD’s new high-end Helios systems, which use its latest MI450 GPUs.Broadcom, which helps many of the biggest AI companies design their own custom chips, has yet to report earnings. But so far, there’s little sign of a frontier slowdown hurting chip sales.Of course, even if AI labs were to significantly scale back their training ambitions, it would take a while to show up in chipmakers’ earnings. Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint Research, told The Verge in September that it would take about six months to see the financial effects of a slowdown, owing to existing computing and memory procurement agreements. The impact could show up sooner in orders placed with chip manufacturers like TSMC.So far, there’s little evidence of that, either: TSMC’s latest sales figures also show continued strength.But there’s another reason a frontier slowdown might not be particularly bad for the chip industry: growing demand for inference, the process of running the AI models we already have.“While one might argue the need for top-end GPUs will reduce with this shift toward inferencing, these workloads will collectively require more compute infrastructure than training,” Shah said. “Overall, it means a net increase in demand for all types of accelerators.”There’s another reason a frontier slowdown might not be particularly bad for the chip industry: growing demand for inference, the process of running the AI models we already have.According to our analysis of the latest data from corporate spending platform Ramp, frontier model families accounted for about 60 percent of token usage among businesses using Ramp in early November — a record high and about three times their share at the start of the year. That includes OpenAI’s Astra and Sol models and Anthropic’s Opus and Fable models.But even as businesses use more AI, their spending is only growing modestly.“It’s not really a demand issue though,” Ara Kharazian, lead economist at Ramp, tells The Verge. “By all measures, companies are using more AI.”Rather, competition among AI model providers is driving down token prices so rapidly that it’s calling OpenAI and Anthropic’s revenue projections into question, Kharazian says.That could prove beneficial for the companies supplying computing power. On Nvidia’s earnings call, Kress said token prices had fallen nearly 60 percent since May, spurring more usage. Meanwhile, rental prices for Nvidia GPUs across generations have gone up.Nvidia and AMD are positioning their most powerful chips for both training and inference, including the demanding workloads created by AI agents.That doesn’t necessarily mean Nvidia will maintain its dominance. As AI companies get more serious about the economics of serving their models to millions of people, they’re increasingly turning to custom chips that can do so more cheaply than general-purpose GPUs. Counterpoint expects shipments of custom AI server processors to surpass those of data center GPUs by 2028.“Pumping the brakes on frontier training won’t shrink the AI chip market but it will simply reallocate the spend,” Shah said.Indeed, on Nvidia’s earnings call, UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri asked Kress whether the company would be willing to sacrifice some of its hefty profit margins as frontier labs increasingly invest in custom chips and prioritize computing efficiency. Kress maintained that Nvidia’s systems justify their pricing and reiterated the company’s gross margin outlook.For companies like Nvidia, the bigger threat may not be that AI companies slow down, but that they find cheaper chips on which to keep going.

history.titleZh: 还记得前沿 AI 暂停吗？芯片公司也不记得了
history.descriptionZh:
文章描绘了一个看似矛盾的局面：一边是前沿AI实验室因安全风险而放缓最强大模型的训练，另一边是AI芯片厂商的业绩和需求继续飙升。今年夏天，OpenAI在AI代理意外入侵Hugging Face、且早期证据显示下一代模型可能独立发现并利用安全漏洞后，暂停了其最大规模的前沿训练任务。9月，Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei呼吁放缓最强模型的推进速度，警告这类模型可能被用于发动网络攻击，也可能变得越来越难以被创造者控制。这一度让投资者担心：如果实验室放缓新模型研发，AI芯片需求是否会受影响，美国芯片股也因此遭遇抛售。

但文章指出，这种放缓看起来非常短暂。OpenAI宣布的只是两周暂停，并在8月底、即10天后重启了训练，不过仍“暂时保留部分较小规模的实验性训练”。Anthropic则在11月发布了Fable和Mythos前沿模型的升级版，强调在编程、推理和视觉能力上的提升。更重要的是，支撑这些进展的芯片厂商业绩比以往更好。

Nvidia在截至10月25日的季度中数据中心收入同比增长110%，达到1076亿美元。公司开始出货其最先进的AI计算系统Vera Rubin NVL72，并称这是“公司历史上最快的产品爬坡”；Rubin平台仅在首个生产出货季度就贡献近200亿美元收入。相关机架已在CoreWeave、Google、Microsoft和Oracle运行，Meta计划扩大Vera Rubin部署，用于训练和运行AI模型及代理。Nvidia还提到Anthropic和OpenAI：Anthropic通过云厂商扩大对Vera Rubin容量的使用，并继续与Nvidia合作设计更贴合其工作负载的未来芯片；OpenAI则采用Nvidia新的Vera CPU。Nvidia临时CEO Colette Kress称，OpenAI和Anthropic等公司的专有模型继续推进前沿，预计主要前沿实验室本财年约占其数据中心收入的15%；Nvidia还将下一财年收入增长预期从70%上调至75%。

AMD也公布了史上最强季度：收入同比增长45%至134亿美元，数据中心销售额几乎翻倍至85亿美元。OpenAI和Anthropic是最早在AMD高端Helios系统上运行工作负载的客户之一，该系统采用最新的MI450 GPU。Broadcom帮助许多大型AI公司设计自研芯片，尚未公布财报，但截至目前，几乎没有迹象显示前沿训练放缓正在伤害芯片销售。文章解释，即便实验室显著收缩训练雄心，由于现有计算和存储采购协议，财务影响大约需要六个月才会显现，而对台积电等芯片制造商的订单影响可能更早；但目前台积电最新销售数据也依然强劲。

从技术逻辑看，文章强调两个关键趋势。第一，训练和推理共同拉动算力。训练是构建和迭代前沿模型，推理则是运行已有模型、服务真实用户和AI代理。Counterpoint研究副总裁Neil Shah表示，转向推理可能减少对顶级GPU的部分需求，但这些工作负载整体上需要比训练更多的计算基础设施，因此对所有类型加速器的需求是净增加。第二，模型调用量在上升，但价格在快速下降。根据Ramp数据，11月初前沿模型系列约占其企业用户token使用量的60%，创历史新高，约为年初份额的三倍，包括OpenAI的Astra、Sol和Anthropic的Opus、Fable等模型；不过企业AI支出只是温和增长。Ramp首席经济学家Ara Kharazian称，这不是需求问题，企业确实在用更多AI，而是模型供应商竞争使token价格迅速下降，甚至令OpenAI和Anthropic的收入预测受到质疑。Nvidia的Kress也表示，自5月以来token价格下降近60%，刺激了更多使用，同时各代Nvidia GPU的租赁价格却在上涨。

产品创新方面，Nvidia和AMD都在把最强芯片同时定位为训练和推理平台，并针对AI代理带来的高要求工作负载优化。Nvidia的Vera Rubin NVL72以整机架、系统级交付形态出现，强调大规模AI计算系统的部署速度和系统性能；AMD则以Helios系统和MI450 GPU切入高端AI计算。另一条重要技术路线是自研定制芯片：随着AI公司越来越重视向数百万用户提供模型的经济性，它们开始采用比通用GPU更便宜、更贴合特定工作负载的定制AI服务器处理器。Counterpoint预计，到2028年，定制AI服务器处理器出货量将超过数据中心GPU。

文章最后指出，对Nvidia等公司而言，更大的威胁可能不是AI公司放缓前沿训练，而是它们找到更便宜的芯片继续推进。Shah总结说，给前沿训练“踩刹车”不会缩小AI芯片市场，只会重新分配支出。Nvidia财报电话会上，UBS分析师Timothy Arcuri询问公司是否愿意在实验室加大定制芯片投资、优先考虑计算效率的情况下牺牲部分高利润率；Kress坚持认为Nvidia系统配得上其定价，并重申毛利率展望。整体来看，前沿训练的安全争议和短暂暂停并未改变AI算力需求的上行趋势，真正影响格局的是训练与推理结构变化、token价格下降带来的用量爆发，以及定制芯片对通用GPU主导地位的长期挑战。

history.title: Leaked Ohio bill could allow AI data center companies to seize private land for their buildouts using eminent domain law
history.description: A leaked Ohio bill could allow data centers to qualify as public utilities for the purpose of eminent domain law, allowing companies to seize private land for building new facilities.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter While Ohioans have rejected the building of new data centers at every turn, they might not have much choice in the future. That's if a newly leaked bill that could allow data centers to be classified as public utilities is allowed to progress. The move would see the list of who can qualify for eminent domain law expanded, moving beyond entities owned or operated by municipal corporations, electric cooperatives, and agencies holding a certificate of public convenience and necessity granted by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. The bill, leaked to WCPO Cincinnati, would add "and an agency holding a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need from the power siting board for constructing an electric transmission line and associated facilities or gas pipeline and its associated facilities."Legal experts have warned that the change could mean a transmission developer, like a power company, would be able to seize land to be used for a data center or a facility that would power one. The writing has been on the wall for a while, too, after it was discovered in June that the Ohio Business Roundtable trade group recommended that lawmakers change eminent domain law to "extend possession authority to energy infrastructure projects once public use and necessity have been established.”This follows a July 2026 report that the government was able to seize private land for new transmission lines needed to power new data centers. The law gives the government the power to take private land without the need for the owner's consent, so long as it is for public use and the owner receives appropriate compensation. The government can also delegate the same land-grabbing power to “private entities or common carriers,” which includes utility companies.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: This is already happening, too. Earlier this year, the largest utility company in Georgia required the removal of 30 residential properties in order to upgrade its grid. Residents claimed that the expansion was to power AI data centers, a fact given more weight by the fact that one such data center was located just a few miles away.Despite this, eminent domain law can still be used for good. Nashville set out to use the same law to block the building of a 69,220-square-foot single-story data center next to a zoo. Nashville Metro Council approved the use of eminent domain as a way to buy the land from a local developer who planned the $700 million data center buildout. history.titleZh: 泄露的俄亥俄州法案可能允许AI数据中心公司利用土地征用权为其建设征用私人土地
history.descriptionZh:
美国俄亥俄州正围绕数据中心用地和供电问题出现新的政策争议。据泄露给辛辛那提媒体WCPO的法案文本，俄亥俄州可能允许数据中心被归类为公共事业，并扩大“国家征用权”（eminent domain）的适用范围。现行法律下，政府可为公共用途征用私人土地，但须给予合理补偿，并可将这一权力授予私营实体或公共承运人，包括公用事业公司。泄露法案拟将可申请征用权的主体扩展至持有俄亥俄州电力选址委员会颁发的“环境兼容性与公共需求证书”、用于建设输电线路及相关设施或天然气管道及相关设施的机构。法律专家警告，这可能意味着输电开发商或电力公司能够征用土地，用于建设数据中心或为数据中心供电的设施。

新闻背景显示，这一变化并非毫无征兆。今年6月，俄亥俄州商业圆桌会议贸易团体曾建议州议员修改征用权法律，在“公共用途和必要性已经确立”的前提下，将占有权扩展至能源基础设施项目。此前还有2026年7月的一份报告称，政府可为新建数据中心所需输电线路征用私人土地。由于数据中心不是传统意义上的公共事业，若法案通过，数据中心项目可能借助“公共需求”和能源基础设施名义获得更强的土地取得能力，从而削弱地方居民和社区对新建数据中心的否决权。

文章还列举了已经发生的案例。今年早些时候，佐治亚州最大公用事业公司为升级电网，要求移除30处住宅物业。居民称，电网扩建是为了给AI数据中心供电，而几英里外正有一座此类数据中心，使这一说法更具说服力。另一方面，征用权也可能被用于阻止数据中心建设。纳什维尔市议会批准使用征用权，从当地开发商手中购买土地，以阻止在动物园旁建设一座69,220平方英尺的单层数据中心；该开发商原计划建设投资7亿美元的数据中心项目。

从技术影响看，这篇新闻并不涉及AI芯片本身的核心技术原理、性能参数或芯片架构创新，而是聚焦AI数据中心快速扩张带来的电力基础设施、土地征用和公共事业监管问题。数据中心，尤其是AI数据中心，需要大规模、稳定的电力供应和输电线路配套，因此输电走廊、变电站和天然气管道等能源基础设施的选址会直接影响项目落地。若数据中心或其供电设施被纳入可征用土地的公共事业范畴，可能加快电网扩容和项目审批，但也可能引发社区反对、土地产权争议和地方治理冲突。文章还提到，亚马逊曾警告680亿美元受阻数据中心威胁美国AI领先地位，美国参议院否决了一项可能保护民众免受AI数据中心导致电费飙升的法案，以及美国政府移除污染相关公众意见要求以压制数据中心反对声音等动向。整体来看，该法案争议的核心是：AI数据中心扩张所需的能源基础设施是否应享有更强公共事业地位，以及这种地位是否会导致私人项目借公共用途之名获得征用私人土地的能力。

history.title: Nvidia says it’s ‘absurd’ to assume it predicted the agentic moment during Vera’s development
history.description: AMD has criticized Nvidia, and to a lesser extent Arm, for claims about creating a CPU designed for agentic AI. Nvidia is pushing back on that characterization, instead saying Vera was designed with “base principles, product intuition, and oftentimes simple allegorical laws of computer science” in a recent interview with Tom’s Hardware.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter One criticism that has emerged of Nvidia’s Vera CPU, driven by AMD, is that Nvidia – and, to a lesser degree, Arm with its AGI CPU – couldn’t have developed an “agentic CPU,” as the chip is often characterized in Nvidia’s marketing materials. Ian Finder, the head of Nvidia’s data center CPU business, pushed back on that criticism in a recent conversation with Tom’s Hardware Premium at SC26, calling the notion that Nvidia somehow knew about the agentic wave four years ago when Vera development began "absurd."“There's a conviction around the design philosophy of the part, right? Am I going to sit here and tell you that we have this magic crystal ball around the agentic moment? That would be absurd, right?” Finder said. “But what we do have as a company, and I think this has been proven out in our track record, is [that] we have design intuition.”Instead of specifically designing Vera for agentic workloads, which would be impossible without a way to see several years into the future, Finder characterized the part by its codesign with Nvidia’s accelerators, something that the team has continued to work on since its first Grace data center CPU. Coming from the assumption that data centers and AI workloads are accelerated (and they largely are), Finder says the co-design approach on the CPU can start in a “conceptually simple space, like what kind of CPU do we need to keep the accelerator fed and happy?”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Although conceptually simple, Finder continually looped back to a particular word to describe aspects of Vera and, to a lesser extent, Grace. “Opinionated” is the word he used, which in the broader context of Vera’s design, shows up in two places. Grace, Finder says, introduced an opinionated memory system with Nvidia’s Scalable Coherency Fabric, while Vera extends that memory system while adding an opinionated microarchitecture, Nvidia’s Olympus core.The picture Finder paints is one of Nvidia starting from scratch in this space, contrasting it with the “legacy constraints” of, presumably, Intel and AMD in particular, who have large pools of customers with specific needs. As we described in our original breakdown of the Olympus architecture in Vera, Nvidia’s goal doesn’t seem to be to steal market share from AMD and Intel, but rather to grab market share in a CPU space that’s vastly accelerating on the back of AI agents. You may like Hot Chips 2026: Nvidia breaks down 88-core Vera CPU AMD VP and chief Zen architect rebuke claims that Nvidia and Arm made CPUs for agentic AI — ‘We didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing’ Modal taps Nvidia Vera CPUs after firm's internal tests show 2x throughput over Intel and AMD chips This “clean sheet of paper” approach, and Nvidia’s codesign, led to some natural assumptions about what the CPU should do. “If we have silicon that needs really, really great single-thread performance, [and] we also need concurrency, then we need to get there with IPC instead of frequency. We need to make sure we have good loaded memory latency. We need to make sure we have a lot of bandwidth, and you start to design something on a clean sheet of paper that's not encumbered by dollar-per-core economics.”Although Finder was clear that Vera’s design didn’t explicitly center around the agents we see today, there were early indications of the workload. “To say that four years ago, when we started putting pen to paper on Vera, [that] we absolutely saw the agentic moment, would [not] be... something I would claim, but we were starting to see the beginnings of tool calling and things like that. We certainly knew what we needed from a head node, and we knew the overall shape of this problem.”As you can see in our Vera CPU benchmarking, the chip doesn’t excel at every workload. And, from the data you can see in our recent AMD EPYC Venice benchmarking, the AMD camp has reclaimed some top spots in several benchmarks. Finder suggests that the superior memory bandwidth of Vera will play a much bigger role in the agentic future as these systems evolve to take better advantage of the compute available.Taking full advantage of the CPUWe need to rewind for just a moment. When the agentic wave hit earlier this year, some characterized the demand as a shift away from GPUs and toward CPUs. That is incorrect. Rather, as is becoming increasingly clear as these agentic workloads progress, these loops can’t take full advantage of the GPUs in a GPU-centric environment, with GPUs often oversubscribed on host nodes. The solution isn’t to get rid of GPUs, of course, nor is it to stop buying them. Rather, it’s to also buy enough CPUs to properly leverage that compute.A portion of the AI industry is focused on tackling the problem of fully utilizing the GPU, Nvidia included. GPUs shouldn’t sit idle for very long (if at all) with the demand today, and they don’t. The challenge today is spinning up these agent sandboxes quickly, within milliseconds, so that the CPU isn’t sitting idle, either. What to read next Benchmarking Nvidia’s Vera CPU for the data center — standalone Vera tested against Granite Rapids-AP and EPYC Turin Standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs land in Oracle Cloud's multi-gigawatt deployment Nvidia claims its Vera CPU can gain up to 39% performance boost via software optimization at SC26 — architectural fine-tuning is needed to fully unleash custom Olympus cores Finder provided an example of using a coding agent. If you’ve used a coding agent before, you’re probably familiar with this process. After prompting, the model will make several small tool calls to read and locate files, passing back to the model in between. These are tiny calls, almost negligible, and the vast majority of the time is spent in the model on the GPU. Then, it may start compiling and testing the project, which is much more bound by the CPU. The GPU, Finder says, isn't sitting idle during that time. It’s being leveraged for another purpose. Finder suggests “that very same thing is going to happen on the CPU.” (Image credit: Nvidia)“The idea that we're just going to say, ‘OK, the CPU can just chill out here, and we're just going to wait,’ that's not going to happen,” Finder said. “What's going to happen is we're going to pack multiple environments together, and we're going to subscribe the socket.”This “very interesting computer science problem,” as Finder described it, is being investigated by AI startups such as Daytona and E2B to spin up and close down agentic sandboxes in milliseconds. And serving more agents will naturally put pressure on the memory system, which is an area where Vera has an edge. “We built a product that does really, really well without such optimizations, but as a design point that really will lean into them when the industry starts to catch up to this,” Finder said.Vera is a fascinating chip, regardless of what you think of it and how it’s presented in marketing materials (from Nvidia itself or elsewhere). Although Grace was the starting point internally, Vera has ridden the wave of agentic to become a much bigger player in the world of CPUs, and Nvidia has already announced that it will follow up with its Rosa CPU featuring the new Rigel microarchitecture. Vera is an opinionated CPU indeed, and time will tell if that opinion is correct.

history.titleZh: 英伟达称，认为其在Vera开发期间预见到智能体时刻是“荒谬的”
history.descriptionZh:
Nvidia数据中心CPU业务负责人Ian Finder在SC26上回应了外界对Vera CPU的一项批评。批评由AMD阵营推动，认为Nvidia——以及程度较轻的Arm及其“AGI CPU”——不可能在四年前就开发出一款如今被Nvidia营销材料称为“agentic CPU”的产品。Finder对Tom’s Hardware Premium表示，称Nvidia四年前就预知“agentic浪潮”的说法“荒谬”；但他强调，Nvidia拥有经业绩证明的设计直觉，Vera并非靠“水晶球”预测今天，而是延续了与加速器协同设计的路线。

Finder解释，Vera的设计出发点不是专门为今天的agent负载定制，而是从Grace数据中心CPU开始就坚持的CPU与加速器协同设计。其逻辑可以概括为一个“概念上简单”的问题：需要什么样的CPU来持续喂饱并满足加速器？在这一思路下，Vera体现出Nvidia所说的“有主见”（opinionated）设计：Grace引入了基于Nvidia Scalable Coherency Fabric的“有主见”的内存系统，Vera进一步扩展该内存系统，并加入“有主见”的微架构——Nvidia Olympus核心。Finder将这种路线描述为从零开始设计，区别于Intel、AMD等拥有大量特定需求客户和“历史包袱”的厂商；Nvidia的目标似乎也不是直接抢夺AMD和Intel的传统市场份额，而是在AI agent推动下快速扩张的加速CPU空间中占据位置。

这种“白纸式”设计和协同设计带来了一些自然假设：如果芯片需要很强的单线程性能，同时又要支持并发，就应通过IPC而非频率来实现；还要保证良好的加载内存延迟和充足带宽。Finder称，团队从四年前开始设计Vera时并未声称已完全看见今天的agentic时刻，但已开始看到tool calling等苗头，也清楚头节点需要什么，以及这类问题的整体形态。换句话说，Vera不是对agentic浪潮的事后贴标签，而是试图用高带宽、低延迟和协同设计来适配加速计算环境。

性能方面，文章指出，从Tom’s Hardware的Vera CPU基准测试看，Vera并非在所有工作负载上都领先；在近期AMD EPYC Venice的基准测试中，AMD阵营在多项测试中重新夺回榜首。Finder则认为，随着agentic系统演进并更好地利用可用算力，Vera更高的内存带宽将发挥更大作用。这里的关键不是“CPU取代GPU”，而是agentic负载需要足够强的CPU来配合GPU：在GPU为中心的环境中，agent循环往往无法充分利用GPU，host节点上的GPU常被超额订阅；解决方案不是停止购买GPU，而是同时配置足够CPU来释放GPU算力。

Finder以编码agent为例说明CPU角色：模型会发起许多很小的工具调用去读取和定位文件，这些调用几乎可以忽略，绝大部分时间花在GPU上的模型中；随后项目编译和测试则更受CPU限制。此时GPU并不会闲置，而是被用于其他任务。Finder预计CPU也会出现类似情况：不会让CPU“闲着等待”，而是把多个环境打包在一起并“订阅”整个socket。Daytona、E2B等AI初创公司正在研究如何在毫秒级启动和关闭agent沙箱，以避免CPU空闲；服务更多agent也会给内存系统带来压力，而这正是Vera的优势所在。Finder称，Vera即使没有这些优化也表现很好，但其设计点会在行业跟上时进一步受益。

整体来看，Vera是一款颇具争议但也很有代表性的芯片：Grace是Nvidia内部起点，Vera则借agentic浪潮成为CPU市场更重要的参与者。Nvidia已宣布后续Rosa CPU将采用新的Rigel微架构。文章最后认为，Vera确实是一款“有主见”的CPU，至于这种判断是否正确，只能由时间验证。

history.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI suffers chemical spill at Mississippi AI data center
history.description: 5,000 to 6,000 gallons of propylene glycol spilled from a SpaceXAI facility in Southaven, Mississippi, before reaching a nearby drainage ditch. State environmental officials have sought to ease the worries of locals, saying there is no risk to their health.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A chemical spill at a SpaceXAI facility in Southaven saw the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) get involved, with between 5,000 and 6,000 gallons of propylene glycol confirmed to have spilled. The chemical is a heat transfer fluid used in a variety of products, such as antifreeze. The chemical ultimately found its way into a drainage ditch, but MDEQ has told residents that there is no immediate threat to their health or safety, according to local news reports.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleHowever, it has also been confirmed that water samples will be collected for further laboratory analysis while workers continue to clean the area and monitor for any further issues. It's also been reported that the chemical was contained to the drainage ditch and did not reach the nearby Horn Lake Creek.It hasn't been a great November for SpaceXAI in Southaven. Earlier this month, it suffered a setback in a lawsuit over pollution in the area caused by its data center. The April 2026 suit targets the company's gas-powered power plant, which is used to supply power for its facility in the Greater Memphis area. It's argued that 27 gas turbines were installed without obtaining the required permits. It's also alleged that the plant could emit more than 5,000 tons of nitrogen oxides and 47 tons of formaldehyde — a cancer-causing chemical — annually. The company has tried to classify the turbines as mobile units to get around the issue, but a judge rejected that manoeuvre.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Clearly aware of the local sentiment towards its presence, SpaceXAI offered a 50% Starlink discount to anyone living near its two Memphis data centers. It also said that it would waive the hardware cost, saving customers $349. SpaceXAI said that, between late June and early September, around 2,000 residents of the greater Memphis and Southaven area had signed up for Starlink connectivity.It was also recently announced that the City of Memphis was ready to make its first major investment as part of its new Community Benefits Ordinance, a fund that uses revenue from SpaceXAI's Colossus 1 facility. Almost $3.3 million will be pumped back into the city to help with housing and neighborhood improvements.
